    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-020",
      "page": 54,
      "ar": "انتشأ منه ( اسم القابض )",
      "en": "From it arises the name the Withholder.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Paired with al-Bāsiṭ: restraining versus extending what sustains a thing, illustrated by water, breath, desire and resources.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/54?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-021",
      "page": 54,
      "ar": "( واسم المختار ) وإن لم يرد في الشرع لكن فعله وأثره ورد",
      "en": "Although the name the Chooser has not come down in revealed law, its action and effect have.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "This is the author's reported criterion, not an external legal ruling verified here. Distinguish an unattested name-form from an attested divine action.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/54?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-022",
      "page": 55,
      "ar": "وأما القائل",
      "en": "As for the Speaker.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Independent *internal* cross-reference at B2007 p55 alongside p52 and p56 makes p38 printed القابل suspect, pending photographed I1876 and manuscript evidence.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/55?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-023",
      "page": 55,
      "ar": "( اسم الحميد ) بمعنى الحامد . وأمّا بمعنى المحمود ، فهو من فروع اسم الحيّ",
      "en": "The Praiseworthy as One Who praises derives from the Speaker; as the One praised, it branches from the Living.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "The same name is affiliated with distinct sources under different active and passive senses: a core example of perspectival derivation.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/55?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-024",
      "page": 55,
      "ar": "فهو الشاكر وهو المشكور",
      "en": "He is at once the One Who gives thanks and the One thanked.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The divine name al-Shakūr is explained with the reception and origin of every grace.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/55?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-025",
      "page": 56,
      "ar": "ثم لما كان أصل التكوين مضافا إلى اسم القائل",
      "en": "Since the origin of bringing-into-being is assigned to the name the Speaker.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Third authorial internal cross-reference supporting the p38 القائل conjecture; do not label as external edition witness.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/56?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-026",
      "page": 56,
      "ar": "فإن الخلق في اللغة جاء على ثلاثة معان ، أحدها : التقدير",
      "en": "In the language, creation has three senses, the first being determination of measure.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The following two are combining and cutting. The three lexical senses explain changing name affiliations.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/56?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-027",
      "page": 56,
      "ar": "فهو من توابع اسم القادر والمريد والقائل والعالم والحيّ والجواد والمقسط على السواء",
      "en": "It follows alike upon the Powerful, Willing, Speaker, Knowing, Living, Generous and Equitable.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "The explicit enumeration of all seven basic names *includes القائل*, powerfully constraining p38 digital القابل; still not a manuscript variant.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/56?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-028",
      "page": 56,
      "ar": "فالقدرة ظاهرة والقوة باطنها",
      "en": "Power is its outward aspect, while strength is its inward aspect.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Farghānī distinguishes qudra at the actual onset of action from quwwa prior to commencement.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/56?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-029",
      "page": 57,
      "ar": "فالخالق يقدّر الصور كلّها ، والباري يصوّر الصور الروحانية والمثالية ، والمصوّر يصور الصور الحسّية",
      "en": "The Creator determines all forms; the Originator fashions spiritual and imaginal forms; the Fashioner forms sensible forms.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Distinguish three creative aspects instead of rendering all as generic 'creation'. The text assigns non-sensory forms specifically to al-Bāriʾ.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/57?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-030",
      "page": 57,
      "ar": "أعني على غير مثال خارج عن علمه تعالى",
      "en": "That is, without a model external to His knowledge.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Explicitly qualifies 'without precedent': creative novelty is not outside the timeless Divine knowledge.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/57?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-031",
      "page": 57,
      "ar": "فكانت هذه الأسماء من وجه من توابع العالم ، ومن وجه من توابع القادر",
      "en": "From one perspective these names are subordinate to the Knowing and from another to the Powerful.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "One name can have multiple conceptual affiliations without contradiction.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/57?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-032",
      "page": 58,
      "ar": "ويشبه أن يكون قدمه كناية عن آخر صورة",
      "en": "It seems possible that His 'foot' stands figuratively for the final form.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Farghānī introduces this as a tentative figurative reading of the ḥadīth, not a binding literal doctrine or a proven sole interpretation.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/58?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-033",
      "page": 58,
      "ar": "إضافة الأحكام والتأثيرات إلى الأسباب ظاهرة ، وإلى مسبّبها باطنة",
      "en": "Attribution of rulings and effects to causes is outwardly manifest, while attribution to their true Causer remains hidden.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Distinguish proximate secondary causes in the world from disclosure of ultimate sovereignty; avoids overreading as denial of causal order.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/58?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-034",
      "page": 58,
      "ar": "وأما الدار الآخرة ، فهي دار كشف وظهور كل شيء على ما هو عليه",
      "en": "The abode of the Hereafter is the abode of disclosure, where everything appears as it truly is.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Explains why al-Malik is specially disclosed as 'Master of the Day of Recompense', although sovereign in both abodes.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/58?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-035",
      "page": 59,
      "ar": "ومن توابع اسم الملك أيضا ( الاسم الحكم )",
      "en": "Among the branches of the King is also the name the Judge.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The Judging name acts through right adjudication and restoring rightful holdings.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/59?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-036",
      "page": 59,
      "ar": "فيتصرّف فيهم تصرف الملاك على ظواهرهم وبواطنهم ، لا تصرف الملوك على ظواهرهم دون بواطنهم",
      "en": "He governs them with ownership over their outward and inward realities, unlike kings who control the outward alone.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Careful contrast between divine ownership of very selves, hearts and spirits versus ordinary political dominion.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/59?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-037",
      "page": 59,
      "ar": "فجميع الصور ملكه والأرواح والقلوب ملكه",
      "en": "All forms belong to Him, and spirits and hearts belong to Him.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Extends ownership to intelligible and spiritual, not merely external jurisdiction.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/59?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-038",
      "page": 60,
      "ar": "ثم يسلمهم إلى ( اسم المعيد ) الذي يعيد الخلق إلى ما ابتدىء منه نزولهم طورا بعد طور",
      "en": "He then hands them over to the name the Restorer, who returns creatures step by step to the source from which their descent began.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Return mirrors descent rank by rank; both concern determinate existence, not spatial travel to an absolute location.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/60?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-039",
      "page": 60,
      "ar": "ومنها إماتة قلبه بالقسوة من حياة الفطرة التي فطر عليها",
      "en": "Among its senses is the death of a person's heart through hardness, extinguishing its primordial life.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "One of several differentiated deaths under al-Mumīt: physical death, death of fitra through hardness, and discipline of the commanding soul.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/60?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR006-040",
      "page": 60,
      "ar": "ومن توابعه أيضا ( الاسم الصبور )",
      "en": "Another of its branches is the name the Forbearing.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Defined below through completion without fatigue and postponing punishment despite the power to prevent opposition.",
      "source_siglum": "B2007",
      "source_url": "https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/60?lang=ar",
      "grade": "modern-printed-digital-selected-locus-checked",
      "historical_print_verified": false,

    }

      "ar": "وعلى المطيعين خفي توفيقه حين أضاف الأفعال والأعمال والجزاء إليهم لطفا بهم",
      "en": "From the obedient He conceals His hidden enabling grace, attributing deeds and their recompense to them in kindness.",

      "en": "He then conceals all these from His friends, so that they witness everything as His favor.",

      "id": "CR007-013",

      "ar": "بحيث يعفو ، أي يندرس ذلك الأثر والحكم",
      "en": "Thus He pardons: the effect and its judgment are effaced.",

      "id": "CR007-014",
      "page": 62,
      "ar": "لأن الرأفة ألطف رحمة باطنة منبعثة من الحبّ والعناية",
      "en": "For raʾfa is a subtler inward mercy arising from love and concern.",
      "disposition": "retain",

    {
      "id": "CR007-015",
      "page": 62,
      "ar": "لانتفاء قابلية قبولهم أثر تلك الرحمة الاختصاصية حال الاقتراف أو خفاء تلك القابلية فيهم عندها",
      "en": "Because their receptivity to particular mercy is missing, or hidden, during the offense.",

      "id": "CR007-016",

    {
      "id": "CR007-017",
      "page": 63,
      "ar": "فإن ما عداهما ممّا يتعلق بهذه النشأة الدنيوية كلّها أمانة وعارية واجب ردّها",
      "en": "All other possessions of this worldly life are a trust or loan required to be returned.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The prior reference is faith and enablement of good works, continuing as eternal gifts.",

    {
      "id": "CR007-018",
      "page": 63,
      "ar": "فالفتح إبداء خير من مضيق خفائية وإظهار سعة ونور من مضيق ظلمة إجمال",
      "en": "Opening is the disclosure of a good from narrow hiddenness, breadth and light from the constriction of undifferentiated obscurity.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Māniʿ here is not a spatial doorway alone: the governing contrast is metaphysical articulation from latent concentration.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",

    {
      "id": "CR007-019",
      "page": 63,
      "ar": "ثم في فتح الصور المثالية من مادة عين الهباء",
      "en": "Next, the opening of imaginal forms from the very matter of primordial dust (habāʾ).",
      "disposition": "retain",

      "en": "Lordship has two judgments: a general one and a particular one.",

      "id": "CR007-038",
      "page": 66,

      "en": "In two respects: the receptive reality and the existence appearing within it.",

    {
      "id": "CR007-039",
      "page": 66,
      "ar": "وأما الحكم الخاص الذي للربوبية هو ما ذكرنا أن كل ما تعيّن وجوده أولا من حضرة اسم كان ذلك الاسم ربّه الخاص",
      "en": "Particular lordship is that everything whose existence first becomes determined in a name's presence has that name as its proper Lord.",

      "id": "CR007-041",
      "page": 67,
      "ar": "ومن قارب الكمّل قابلية واستعدادا وحيطة وكلية وذوقا وشهودا",
      "en": "Those approaching the perfected in receptivity, preparation, inclusiveness, universality, taste and witnessing.",

      "id": "CR007-042",
      "page": 67,

      "en": "Or from rivers branching from their branches, then their streams and channels.",

    {
      "id": "CR007-043",
      "page": 67,
      "ar": "فبحسب الاستعداد يكون تعيّنهم أولا ومرجعهم آخرا",
      "en": "Their first determination and final return accord with their preparedness.",
      "disposition": "retain",

    {
      "id": "CR007-044",
      "page": 67,

      "en": "Our Prophet Muḥammad has the supreme spring: the first self-disclosure, his light first and his Lord in a second regard.",

      "en": "Its words are the essential names called the Keys of the Unseen.",

      "id": "CR007-046",

      "en": "They come to an end on returning to the first self-disclosure.",

      "id": "CR007-047",
      "page": 68,
      "ar": "فإن الوجود الذي هو عين الرحمة التي وسعت كل شيء ، وهو عين الرحمن له جهتان",
      "en": "Existence, identical with all-encompassing mercy and the All-merciful, has two aspects.",

      "critical_note": "The two aspects concern bestowing and being bestowed, not two entities with rival essences.",

    {
      "id": "CR007-048",
      "page": 68,
      "ar": "إحداهما : أنه مفيض على الحقائق الكونية لإظهار الكمالات المتعلقة بها",
      "en": "In the first, it bestows upon cosmic realities, disclosing their perfections.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Agentive consideration of existence as effusion.",

      "id": "CR007-049",
      "page": 68,
      "ar": "وأما جهته الثانية : كونه مفاضا مضافا إلى الكائنات في المراتب الكونية",
      "en": "In the second, it is bestowed and predicated of creatures within their cosmic ranks.",

      "id": "CR007-050",
      "page": 68,
      "ar": "فلا جرم كلمات اللّه في النزول والتعلّق بالأبدية لا تتناهى",
      "en": "Hence God's words are inexhaustible in descent and their relation to everlastingness.",

      "critical_note": "This and return's termination are not inconsistent because they refer to distinct directions.",

    {

      "en": "The letter hāʾ with wāw generally indicates Essence in the outward aspect of the Presence of Identity.",

    {

      "page": 103,

      "en": "That true locus is corporeally the purified, most balanced Muhammadan temperament and inwardly his pure, Godwary heart.",

      "en": "All of these are intelligible forms of the considerations of oneness, apparent relative to the Real insofar as they are relations.",

      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The higher universal form is analogized to the Qurʾān, completing the cosmic-book analogy.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "111",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-021",
      "page": 112,
      "ar": "فتلك النقطة الاعتدالية هي نقطة الولاية لقربها من أحدية الغيب المطلق",
      "en": "That point of equilibrium is the point of sainthood, because of its nearness to the unicity of the absolute Unseen.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Wilāya arises as spiritual centrality, not merely office or institutional authority.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "112",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-022",
      "page": 112,
      "ar": "فكان في هذا معنى القرب",
      "en": "In this lies the meaning of nearness.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Root derivation from walāʾ and tawālī is an authorial etymological argument.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "112",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-023",
      "page": 113,
      "ar": "فالنقطة الوسطية الاعتدالية الوحدانية ... إنما هي حقيقة النبوّة",
      "en": "The unifying middle point of balance corresponds to the reality of prophethood.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "A related but distinct centre from the wilāya-centre of the preceding page.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "113",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-024",
      "page": 113,
      "ar": "والنبوّة إن اعتبرت مهموزة ، فهي من الإنباء الإخبار",
      "en": "Prophethood, when the word is pronounced with hamza, derives from informing and giving news.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "One of two lexical derivations, the other from elevation; avoid falsely asserting a sole lexical origin.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "113",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-025",
      "page": 114,
      "ar": "فالنبيّ إذن صاحب إذن إلهي",
      "en": "Thus a prophet is one who possesses divine authorization.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "In the author's functional distinction between prophet and messenger.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "114",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-026",
      "page": 114,
      "ar": "والرسول صاحب أمر ، أي مأمور بالدعوة والتبليغ",
      "en": "The messenger possesses a command: he is ordered to summon and deliver the message.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "A particular doctrinal criterion in Farghānī, not necessarily a consensus definition in kalām.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "114",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-027",
      "page": 115,
      "ar": "غير أن آدم عليه السلام لما كان صاحب هبوط ونزول",
      "en": "But Adam—peace be upon him—was the one of descent and coming down.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Contrasted with Muḥammadan return/ascent, not a moral deficiency in Adam.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "115",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-028",
      "page": 115,
      "ar": "فلا جرم من لدنّ آدم إلى محمد صلى اللّه عليه وسلم كانت النبوّة ظاهرة ، والولاية مخفيّة مندرجة فيها",
      "en": "Thus from Adam to Muḥammad prophethood was outwardly manifest and sainthood hidden within it.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Descent-era aspect of the author's prophetic history, not a rejection of sainthood among earlier prophets.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "115",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-029",
      "page": 116,
      "ar": "فكان اجتماع حقيقة الولاية مع حقيقة النبوّة فيه على السواء",
      "en": "In him the reality of sainthood and prophethood met in equal balance.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Balanced aspects in the Muhammadan reality.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "116",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-030",
      "page": 116,
      "ar": "ولمّا كان صلى اللّه عليه وسلم صاحب عود ورجوع وعروج ؛ كما أن آدم كان صاحب هبوط ونزول",
      "en": "Since he was the one of return and ascent, as Adam had been the one of descent.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The opposite poles are typological, not competing actual persons.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "116",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-031",
      "page": 117,
      "ar": "فلا جرم ختم به النبوّة ، فلا نبيّ بعده أصلا",
      "en": "Hence prophethood was sealed by him: absolutely no prophet follows him.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Author explicitly affirms finality of prophethood.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "117",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-032",
      "page": 117,
      "ar": "كلّهم كانوا أولياء وأقطابا مندرجا حكم النبوّة في ولايتهم",
      "en": "All were saints and poles with the judgment of prophethood contained within their sainthood.",
      "disposition": "crux",
      "critical_note": "This distinguishes spiritual inheritance from any new prophetic commission; careful theological note required.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "117",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-033",
      "page": 118,
      "ar": "كان القرآن جامعا جميع الطرق والأحكام",
      "en": "The Qurʾān comprehends all paths and determinations.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Farghānī's theology of comprehensive revelation, not a claim every physical fact is directly stated.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "118",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-034",
      "page": 118,
      "ar": "يفهم ويستنبط ويستخرج من عباراته وإشاراته ودلالاته ومفهوماته",
      "en": "One understands, derives and extracts from its verbal expressions, allusions, indications and conceived meanings.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "The four exegetical channels are not identical; important for the planned tafsīr linkage.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "118",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-035",
      "page": 119,
      "ar": "محتاج في كل آن إلى مدد وجودي يرجح جانب بقاء ذلك الشخص على فنائه",
      "en": "At every instant a person needs existential assistance that gives preponderance to remaining over passing away.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Explicit notion of continued actualization, distinct from metaphysical dependence understood only at origin.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "119",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-036",
      "page": 119,
      "ar": "ووصول هذا المدد دائما مع الآنات عبارة عن الخلق الجديد",
      "en": "The continuous arrival of this assistance with the instants is what is meant by renewed creation.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "This provides an especially direct definition of khalq jadīd, parallel to p66 and p73.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "119",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-037",
      "page": 120,
      "ar": "موجب إعراضه وغفلته عن موجده الحق تعالى",
      "en": "It brings about his turning away and heedlessness of the Real who originates him.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The account links impediments in formative descent to spiritual veiling.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "120",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-038",
      "page": 120,
      "ar": "والتسويلات والتسويفات النفسانية والشيطانية",
      "en": "And the soul's and devil's deceptive suggestions and procrastinations.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Lexically distinguish taswīl (persuasive embellishment of vice) from taswīf (putting off action).",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "120",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-039",
      "page": 121,
      "ar": "فالشريعة هي المعينة لبعض تلك الأقوال والأفعال والحركات والسكنات",
      "en": "The Law specifies speech, actions, movements and stillness conducive to removal of veils.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "Sharīʿa is the universal regimen; individualized spiritual treatment is separately supplied by experienced guides.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "121",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-040",
      "page": 121,
      "ar": "وعلماء الطريقة والحقيقة الذين هم كبار المشايخ وأطباء تلك العلل والأمراض المعنوية",
      "en": "Those learned in the path and the truth—the great masters—are physicians of spiritual maladies.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "The comparison is explicitly therapeutic and analogical.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "121",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-041",
      "page": 122,
      "ar": "فعلى هذا يكون أهم المهمات للسالك الطالب ... حصول شيخ مرشد",
      "en": "Thus the foremost concern for the seeking traveller is obtaining a guiding master.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Farghānī's own normative programme, not a neutral universal condition of religion.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "122",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-042",
      "page": 122,
      "ar": "ومظهرا عرفانا كسبيّا ظنّه كشفيّا شهوديّا",
      "en": "And displaying acquired knowledge that he mistakes for unveiled, witnessed gnosis.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Central epistemic warning: acquired/scholarly knowledge may be misidentified as direct spiritual realization.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "122",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-043",
      "page": 123,
      "ar": "ولظاهر هذه البرزخية حكم إجمال وحكم تفصيل",
      "en": "The outer aspect of this intermediacy has a comprehensive judgment and a differentiated judgment.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Maintains barzakh's structural polarity.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "123",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-044",
      "page": 123,
      "ar": "ومزاج سائر الكمل والخلفاء وأولي العزم من الرسل والأقطاب من الأولياء المحمديين هو صورة البرزخية الثانية",
      "en": "The temperament of the other perfected vicegerents and resolute messengers, and Muhammadan poles, images the second intermediacy.",
      "disposition": "annotate",
      "critical_note": "Farghānī's spiritual anthropological hierarchy; a technical rather than empirical temperament claim.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "123",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-045",
      "page": 124,
      "ar": "ففي الرتبة الأولى الكونية تلبس بلباس مظهر روحاني",
      "en": "In the first cosmic rank it wears the form of a spiritual manifestation.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Three ranks: spiritual, imaginal and sensible.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "124",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-046",
      "page": 124,
      "ar": "وهو الذي قامت به الفطرة الأصلية التي فطر الخلق عليها",
      "en": "It is the basis of the primordial disposition upon which creatures are fashioned.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "Fitra is associated with the unitary heart in all forms, not exclusively adults.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "124",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-047",
      "page": 125,
      "ar": "حتى غفلت عن أصل فطرتيها المذكورتين",
      "en": "Until the soul forgot the origins of its two primordial dispositions.",
      "disposition": "revise",
      "critical_note": "The two fitras here are corporeal and spiritual, not two religious communities.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",
      "source_url": "https://alshrefalm7sy.ahlamontada.com/t3214",
      "source_page_marker": "125",
      "source_grade": "secondary-online-retranscription-of-modern-edited-Arabic; selected authorial span; no original print or manuscript photograph",
      "grade": "derivative-Arabic-to-working-English-selected-locus-review",
      "historical_print_verified": false,
      "manuscript_verified": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CR010-048",
      "page": 125,
      "ar": "انحرفت أخلاقها وأوصافها بالميل إمّا إلى جانب إفراط أو طرف تفريط",
      "en": "It inclines either to the extreme of excess or to the opposite of deficiency.",
      "disposition": "retain",
      "critical_note": "A virtue-ethical balance model underlies spiritual pathology.",
      "source_siglum": "D-Forum-B2007-derivative",

# Farghānī — Stage XVI critical-edition handoff: original-resolution print and p52 correction
**9 November 2026 | exact active research status**.

## Project and inherited corpus

Saʿīd al-Dīn al-Farghānī, *Muntahā al-madārik*, Arabic four-foundation introduction, Beirut B2007 printed pp18–143 plus separate prefatory supplement pp144–145. A **128-page-labelled English WORKING draft** is preserved in `editorial/WORKING_TRANSLATION_18_145.md`; it is **not** a fully source-proofread critical translation. The bilingual selected-locus reader includes **559 authorial Arabic–English records** distributed across all 128 B2007 printed page labels, divided into **283 earlier source checks from digitized edited Beirut Arabic pp18–60** and **276 lower-grade checks using a derivative forum retranscription on pp61–145**. No whole modern printed page has been exhaustively checked against an independently collated manuscript.

**Earlier Stage XV** found 14 photographic 1876 PRINT-to-modern-digital/derivative bounded comparisons (six differences, eight agreements), including p38 `القابل` confirmed, and p48 `بسبحات` (“splendours”) against the later digital `بسبحاب`. The earlier complete 559-record master and report remain unchanged in `editorial/CUMULATIVE_SELECTED_BILINGUAL_015.md`, `editorial/I1876_COLLATION_STAGE_015.md`, and `editorial/STAGE_HANDOFF_CRITICAL_015.md`.

## New Stage XVI work actually performed

1. **Reactivated the existing GNAMMA IIIF original-resolution capture workflow**, extending its selected canvas list to **12,13,14,17,20,22,24,32,36,42,43**. Successfully retrieved and archived **eleven 2200-pixel-wide photographed leaves** of the 1876 PRINT, under `facsimile-I1876-hires/images/`. Machine-readable source URLs, image sizes, and SHA-256 are in `facsimile-I1876-hires/IIIF_SELECTED_HIRES_MANIFEST.json`. GitHub Actions **run 42661161348 succeeded**, artifact **13693469212**, digest `sha256:45b25038fe984f4e1d1636dc9a365e751d230c4b12be9490f35dcb069abb2a75`; the short-lived GitHub Actions artifact expires **9 December 2026**, whereas the eleven images are also committed to the repository.
2. **Resolved previously unverified observation `I1876-OBS15-PENDING`:** a full-resolution actual historical 1876 printed p32, IIIF scan36, visibly reads **تفرّع ( اسم الحكم ) منه**. Modern **online digitized B2007 p52** reads **تفرّع ( سم الحكيم ) منه**, lacking `ا` in `اسم` and replacing **al-Ḥakam** (Judge) with **al-Ḥakīm** (Wise). This is a material print-vs-digital difference, **NOT** a medieval manuscript variant and **NOT YET** proof of the wording of the physical B2007 print. Image `facsimile-I1876-hires/images/scan_0036.jpg`, **2200 × 3370 pixels**, SHA-256 **`8a5f2a25fb93cc6560442dd7c0b9f8e9499f833df7b5c33153e12ea4c0463950`**. The original manifestation source is https://sites.dlib.nyu.edu/viewer/api/image/books/princeton_aco000264/36/full/2200,/0/default.jpg.
3. **Changed the provisional edited Arabic/English in-place where appropriate, WITHOUT overwriting diplomatic modern reading:** `data/critical-pass-006-p48-49-51-60.js`, CR006-015, retains B2007 `ar: تفرّع ( سم الحكيم ) منه`, adds `edited_ar: تفرّع ( اسم الحكم ) منه`, and corrects `en` to “From it branches the name **the Judge** (*al-Ḥakam*).” `historical_print` links source photo and photographic apparatus. `editorial/WORKING_TRANSLATION_18_145.md` now likewise says “the Judge” on p52, with a dated source note.
4. **Recorded context and facing pages:** `editorial/I1876_P32_NAME_SEQUENCE_016.md` maps the original I1876 p32 sequence across modern B2007 pp52–53. Names arising under the Knowing (al-ʿAlīm) include al-Ḥakam; the name is also placed under Sovereignty at B2007 p59, with different conceptual regard (*iʿtibār*). This is interpretation, not proof of which manuscript family preserves authorial text. Page32 sequence contains the names **al-Muḥīṭ, al-Wāsiʿ, al-Shahīd, al-Wājid, al-Laṭīf, al-Nūr, al-Raqīb, al-Ḥakam, al-Ḥafīẓ, al-Muhaymin, al-Muʾmin**, then the section on al-Murīd and derivatives including al-Hādī, al-Muḍill, al-Rashīd. The name-index is **not** claimed to be a full diplomatic Arabic transcription.
5. **New stage publications:** `editorial/I1876_COLLATION_CUMULATIVE_006.json` provides all **15 exact photographed PRINT comparisons**, **seven print-vs-digital differences** and **eight agreements** across **14 distinct historic printed page labels**. `editorial/I1876_COLLATION_STAGE_016.md` gives the p52 proof and original source metadata. `editorial/CUMULATIVE_SELECTED_BILINGUAL_016.md` preserves all **559** annotated excerpts with the p52 textual correction and English change. The coverage ledger and reader are updated; the old XV record remains in its own version for auditability.

## Current evidentiary totals (no inflation)

- Complete English page-labelled introductory WORKING draft: **128/128 printed pages**, NOT definitive.
- Selected Arabic–English bilingual records: **559**, of which **283** modern digitized edited source excerpt checks and **276** *derivative modern retyped* excerpt checks. All 128 page labels have a checked excerpt, but **zero entire printed pages** independently collated line-by-line.
- Historical 1876 photographed original PRINT source: **15 bounded exact phrase comparisons** at **14 distinct historical printed page labels**, **7 differences** against later modern digital/derivative material, **8 bounded agreements**; these are NOT 14 whole pages.
- Actual medieval handwritten manuscript folios examined: **0**; genuinely authenticated manuscript variants: **0**. Complete critical Arabic text and source family stemma: **not yet established**.

## Specific open textual problems

- B2007 physical print p52 **`اسم الحكم` / `سم الحكيم`**: 1876 high-resolution PRINT definitely reads `اسم الحكم`; require actual photographic B2007 **printed** page to determine if the online text is at fault; then MS witness check.
- B2007 p38 **`القابل`**: the original 1876 print agrees; no longer promote the conjecture `القائل` without manuscripts.
- B2007 p48 **`بسبحات` vs online `بسبحاب`**: older 1876 photo yields “splendours”; English corrected, MS uncollated.
- B2007 p41 `عماء` ḥadīth linguistic and transmission complexities; p63 `مشيمة` anatomical/imagery, p73 `لكونه عرضا` and exact referent/creation doctrine, p87 `محضة` printed crux, p97 angels' apparent defects in spiritual exegesis require independent review.
- B2007 pages 61–145: selected English checking so far mostly based on modern **derivative**, not verified against the physical printed Beirut volume.

## Exact next executable work (not repeated translation of the working draft)

**Primary priority** obtain a readable photographed **physical B2007 pp38,48,52,61–65** and collate line by line with the I1876 printed photographs, with a page/line concordance that does not equate different pagination systems. **Parallel priority** obtain actual independent manuscript folios, starting with C1107 (Carullah 1107), R670 (Koca Ragıp Paşa 670), K273 (Kadızademehmed 273), ideally also F3966 and Y706. Confirm shelfmark, folio, date, completeness, copy relationships; only **actual witnessed variant readings** may enter manuscript apparatus. Then produce a *continuous* Arabic lemma text with full English checking and specialist review. The later verse commentary is separate from the four-foundation introduction and should not be marked complete.

**Restart instruction:** read this file, the **I1876_COLLATION_CUMULATIVE_006.json**, the **CRITICAL_COVERAGE_REGISTER.json**, and **WORKING_TRANSLATION_18_145.md**, then target the actual photographed B2007 p52 or first manuscript folio. Do NOT re-run secondary excerpt generation or count scans as manuscripts. Archive the stage before further work so another interrupted chat can resume.

# Farghānī Stage XVII — 2007 physical-source candidate integrity audit
**11 November 2026 | evidence class: external source-link vetting; not printed-text collation**

## Verified bibliographic target
Saʿīd al-Dīn al-Farghānī, *Muntahā al-madārik fī sharḥ Tāʾiyyat Ibn al-Fāriḍ*, edited by ʿĀṣim Ibrāhīm al-Kayyālī, Beirut: Dār al-Kutub al-ʿIlmiyya, 2007. Publisher ISBN **9782745146120**; publisher catalogue: https://www.al-ilmiyah.com/details?id=978-2-7451-4612-0 and https://books.google.com/books?id=lS50DwAAQBAJ.

## Disqualified as independent B2007 evidence
Some external third-party pages describe `https://archive.org/download/lis_q115/lisanarb.com_q1508.pdf` as the 2007 Farghānī edition. Direct PDF access redirected to an unavailable mirror; **the actual PDF pages were NOT viewed**. However the Internet Archive's accessible associated OCR transcript at https://archive.org/stream/lis_q115/lisanarb.com_q1508_djvu.txt repeatedly labels book leaves **شرح داود بن محمود القيصري**, i.e. the separate commentary on the Tāʾiyya attributed to Dāwūd al-Qayṣarī, not Farghānī's *Muntahā* (OCR transcript around its lines 6430–6435; also later repeated headings). The OCR's printed bibliographic data appear incompatible with the target ISBN, but OCR is imperfect and cannot by itself prove the entire PDF's identity. **Provisional determination: strong mismatch; disqualify the URL for comparison until actual cover/title images are independently verified.** Do not cite its OCR as Farghānī's 2007 printed text, and do not present it as the source of any corrected textual locus.

A different archive link from https://www.nafahat-tarik.com/2015/03/sufism_11.html points to `https://archive.org/download/lis02029/01.pdf` and may be more promising, but fetching returned HTTP 403 and no page images were inspected. **Its title and image contents remain UNVERIFIED.**

## Valid current printed source, grade and remaining lacuna
- Actual photographed **Istanbul 1293/1876 printed volume I**: https://sites.dlib.nyu.edu/viewer/books/princeton_aco000264/1?embed=1&lang=en ; eleven select original-resolution photographed leaves already archived in `../facsimile-I1876-hires/images/`.
- Modern online edited Arabic `B2007-digitized`: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9606/18?lang=ar ; its web transcription is NOT proof of physical 2007 paper characters.
- Core B2007 p52 crux: digital `سم الحكيم` against photographed 1876 printed p32 `اسم الحكم`. Earlier photographed-source comparison already recorded; **no new source reading is established in this audit**.
- Source authenticity for historical photo p34 *Cloud-like Presence* `الحضرة العمائية` already checked under I1876 p18/scan22, critical record CR004-040; 2007 digital `الحضرة العملية`; the Stage XVII continuous reader now reflects this verified older-print lemma.

## Strict conclusion
**0 newly inspected physical Beirut 2007 printed leaves; 0 new independent manuscript folios, 0 new authorial variants.** The evidence grade and cumulative critical counters stay unchanged: 128-page English working draft; 559 selected Arabic–English records; 15 original-photograph 1876 PRINT comparisons (7 digital differences, 8 bounded agreements); 0 manuscript variants. The next chat must source a verifiably pictured B2007 p52, not assume any third-party “download” link identifies its payload correctly.

<main id="fr-main"><article id="document"><section class="b2007-page" data-part-start="Foundation I · Essence and names" id="b2007-p18" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p18"><h3 id="title-b2007-p18">B2007 p. 18 · The hidden treasure and first disclosure</h3>

<p><strong>First foundation.</strong> Concerning the ranks of the Essence; the differentiation from it of the names and attributes; the manner in which the branches of those names and attributes arise from their roots; an explanation of the meanings of the ninety-nine names; and the arising from them of all the other names, whether subtle or great.</p>
<p>In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. It is related from the Messenger of God—may God bless him and grant him peace—that he said: God, mighty and exalted, said: “I was a hidden treasure, and I loved to be known; therefore I created creatures so that I might be known.”</p>
<p>Know—may God strengthen you with sound understanding—that in this divine saying the hidden treasure is a figurative designation for the innermost depth of the Unseen, the nondelimitation of the most holy Essence and the inwardness of the eternal divine Identity. The comparison arises because a treasure is something concealed and guarded, a secret held in reserve containing jewels of great worth. Some are so valuable that they are protected, jealously retained, and reserved for their possessor; others, while still precious, may be made available or exchanged privately or publicly.</p>
<p>When a treasure is to be disclosed, it is presented first as a whole, so that it is recognized as a treasure and appears to its finder in its own place. It is then presented a second time in a manner that distinguishes the most precious jewels from the others; some are removed from their place according to a wisdom perceived by their finder—for example, to display a perfection that includes wealth, adornment, and liberality.</p>
<p>Analogically—and God possesses the supreme similitude in the heavens and the earth, while He is the Mighty, the Wise, utterly exalted above any comparison of likeness, configuration, or representation—the innermost reality of the most holy Presence is the concealed Unseen, the safeguarded secret, more inward than anything inward. Its hiddenness comprehends the precious jewels of the essential divine names. Some of these names He reserves in His hidden mystery, known only by Him and by one whose separateness and individual self-standing have been lifted away, among the most perfect of those who attain perfection.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p19" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p19"><h3 id="title-b2007-p19">B2007 p. 19 · The names, love, and the negative knowledge of the Essence</h3>

<p>Those perfected persons participate in the display of the first determination and first self-disclosure for the realization of the nobler essential perfection signified by “I loved to be known.” The treasure also contains the precious jewels of the names of attributes, disclosure of which is graciously permitted to each suitably prepared person characterized by them or fully realized in them. It further comprehends the names of acts, whose benefit and influence are general, and whose judgments and effects flow through every cosmic rank. These ranks are the loci of the completion of the perfection of the names, the desired aim signified by “I created creatures so that I might be known.”</p>
<p>The expression “I was” tells of a determination preceded by nondelimitation. For the first-person marker implies the speaker's determination within himself and his appearing when he speaks of himself. The description “a hidden treasure,” by contrast, indicates His unseen and unconditioned character. As such, He falls under no determinate judgment with respect to this unseen nondelimitation, nor can knowledge, considered from His determinations, encompass Him in that respect. Absolute hiddenness entails all this. Since hiddenness is predicated of “I was,” the nondelimited and unseen are understood to precede that determination—but this is a <strong>precedence of rank, not a precedence of time</strong>; there is neither morning nor evening for God.</p>
<p>The words “then I loved” announce an original inclination joining the hiddenness and manifestation just mentioned. But there is nothing there beyond the determination that is itself unity; accordingly this inclination is identical with it.</p>
<p>The words “that I might be known” point to the manifestation of what was hidden. The words “I created creatures so that I might be known” make it understood that the determining of determined things, both in knowledge and in existence, follows that inclination and is ordered to its object: the manifestation arising through that determination. This is so that the perfection of manifestation may be realized in distinction and detail, and its effect may extend to the determiner and to what is determined. Such succession is essential rather than temporal; it is also a succession in knowledge and existence, considered in relation to the eternal Determiner who knows, and to His essential and attributive knowledge. For His knowledge is His very existence. Understand, and—if God wills—you will discover the red sulphur and the greatest treasure.</p>
<p>Know also that the innermost reality of the most holy Essence, the unseen depth of Identity, nondelimitation and pre-eternity—which contains within it the character of everlastingness—cannot be witnessed, understood, known or apprehended under the consideration of determination; nor can it come under any determinate judgment whatsoever, except perhaps the negative judgment that it cannot be known. Even such a negative judgment can be arrived at in only one of two ways. The first is a divine report concerning this truth.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p20" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p20"><h3 id="title-b2007-p20">B2007 p. 20 · The two limits of knowledge and the first journey</h3>

<p>The first way is by divine disclosure that no knowledge can encompass Him, as in God's saying, “They do not encompass Him in knowledge” (Qurʾān 20:110), and the expression “I was a hidden treasure,” and similar utterances.</p>
<p>The second way is that the most perfect apprehensions and sciences, and the most expansive acts of witnessing and understanding, are brought to a halt before Him and confess their incapacity, limitation and bewilderment. They acknowledge that beyond the utmost reach of their apprehension and the farthest horizon of their witnessing lie oceans whose currents confound the understanding of every diver who has reached a station, and wildernesses whose depths and innermost secrets bewilder the knowledge of every knowing traveler. These are the highest end and most worthy object of seeking.</p>
<p>The Prophet—may God bless him and grant him peace—indicated as much in his supplication: “I cannot number the praise due to You,” that is, I cannot reach everything that belongs to You. He also spoke in his prayer of names “which You have reserved in the hidden mystery with You,” and was reported to have said, “My Lord, increase me in bewilderment concerning You,” along with similar sayings.</p>
<p>Whenever something belonging to these divine perfections is known, witnessed or apprehended in an outward, inward or all-comprehensive self-disclosure along the journey of love and in the nearness of supererogatory devotion—where disciplined journeying precedes attraction and annihilation precedes abiding—the opening may reveal that the self-disclosing Real is the instrument by which the servant apprehends.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p21" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p21"><h3 id="title-b2007-p21">B2007 p. 21 · Two journeys; the two considerations of unity</h3>

<p>This belongs to the sense of the saying “I became his hearing and his sight: by Me he hears and by Me he sees.” In the corresponding journey of the beloved, the nearness of obligatory acts, where attraction precedes disciplined travel and original abiding precedes annihilation, it becomes clear that the servant to whom disclosure occurs is an instrument for the apprehension of the self-disclosing Real, as expressed in the attribution to God, on the tongue of His servant, “God hears the one who praises Him.”</p>
<p>At the consummation of the two journeys, where both judgments are brought together at their beginning and end, each may be apprehender and instrument, either alternately or in a single state together. This is indicated by “You did not throw when you threw, but God threw” (Qurʾān 8:17). In every case, such knowing, witnessing, disclosure and apprehension concern His determination, His will and His sacred knowledge of His most holy Essence <em>under the consideration of its oneness</em> (<em>wāḥidiyya</em>), not under the consideration of its nondelimitation and unicity (<em>aḥadiyya</em>). Apprehending or witnessing Him under the consideration of His determination and knowledge is not forbidden; rather, it is left to His will: “They encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills” (Qurʾān 2:255).</p>
<p>The unity from which unicity and oneness arise is identical with His Essence; it is no added attribute or qualification. This unity has two original, primary considerations. The first is the complete removal of considerations from it. Under this consideration the Essence is named <em>aḥad</em>—One in unicity—and the name is related to the Essence's hiddenness, nondelimitation and pre-eternity. Accordingly, the name <em>aḥad</em> is more properly associated with negation than with positive affirmation.</p>
<p>The second consideration is the establishment for it of infinitely many considerations while they remain included within it at the first rank of the Essence. The greater part of the differentiation of their determinations is realized at the second rank, both of which will be explained shortly. Examples are the relations of being half, third and quarter, which are included in the one considered here. From such relations the numbers arise in the orders of existence, and the determinate twos, threes and fours arise from these considerations, as when one says that one is half of two, a third of three, a quarter of four, and so on.</p>
<p>Under this second consideration the Essence is called <em>wāḥid</em>, a positive rather than a negative name. These considerations cannot be ascribed to the name <em>aḥad</em>, either in reality or by ordinary linguistic usage.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p22" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p22"><h3 id="title-b2007-p22">B2007 p. 22 · Inclusion and the first articulation of known things</h3>

<p>The realities of those considerations are established under the name of the truly One at the first rank of the Essence and are essentially included within it, just as their examples and images are included within the numerical one whose effect we observe here. In neither rank does such inclusion damage or contradict the simplicity of the one. What pertains to the consideration of oneness is the Essence's manifestation, existence and everlastingness, just as what pertains to the consideration of unicity is its inwardness and pre-eternity.</p>
<p>There is no difference or otherness between these two considerations, nor between any one consideration of oneness and another at the first rank. Difference and otherness are judgments belonging to multiplicity and its opposition to unity. At that rank there is no multiplicity contrary to unity: this unity is itself the origin of every unity and multiplicity we understand here as different. As stated, no difference, otherness or distinction obtains at the first rank of the most holy Essence.</p>
<p>No one understands the lifting of such otherness at that Presence unless, in state and station, he has risen beyond restriction by ranks whose determinations impose the judgments of multiplicity on those who inhabit them. Because otherness is overcome at the first rank, some of the great realized people of God have judged that <em>al-wāḥid al-aḥad</em> is a single compound name, like certain other compound proper names.</p>
<p>Know next that these considerations, established for unity there and included in the one at the first rank, are judged there to be the Essence itself: whatever is ascribed to the Essence in respect of comprehensiveness and containing the whole is ascribed likewise to each of them, according to that rank. If we consider them through their appearances, forms and effects, some prove to be universals and first principles, comparable to supreme genera. They are the meanings denoted by words pointing to the realities of the essential names: the Keys of the Unseen, the One-in-Unicity, the inward meanings of the names Allāh, al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, and the comprehensive meanings of the pronominal names.</p>
<p>Other such considerations, viewed through their manifestations and effects, resemble subordinate genera, species within them, and so on down to individuals and the most narrowly particular levels. On their basis the everlasting Presence is described as having indefinitely many determinations and delimitations. All these are established in intelligible forms at the second rank, some as individuated contents and others by inclusion within classes and species.</p>
<p>Many are also determined and fixed in the Preserved Tablet, where they acquire spiritual existential forms, collectively and in detail, whose manifestation extends to the Resurrection. They are differentiated from it in existential ranks, comprehensively in the Throne and in detail in the Footstool, in one act, and successively from these in the elements and the heavens down to the last ranks.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p23" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p23"><h3 id="title-b2007-p23">B2007 p. 23 · Concealed affairs and the limits of manifested knowledge</h3>

<p>The detailed cosmic ranks culminate in the world of being, as imaginal and sensory reality, and in the abodes of the world, the intermediate state and the hereafter. To this point extend all the acts of witnessing, apprehension and unveiling attained by the perfected and the friends of God. The lower and higher among them are alike regarding this limit.</p>
<p>Nevertheless, in the eternal unseen Presence there may perhaps be, with regard to these universals and particulars, concealed things and hidden states which have not yet been determined either in the second rank or in the Preserved Tablet. They are therefore not known or assigned a judgment until they receive determination and occur within the existential ranks gradually, through moments. These belong to the innermost depth of the judgments of the essential Unseen, whose hidden character is overcome and preceded by essential mercy.</p>
<p>For this reason they occasion fear and reverent awe, as indicated by the Qurʾānic saying: “Say: I am no innovation among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you” (Qurʾān 46:9). The Prophet's reported statement, uttered out of concern, “Would that Muhammad's Lord had not created Muhammad,” is also taken to allude to them from one perspective.</p>
<p>Yet insofar as his state was determined in the Presence of knowledge and in the Preserved Tablet, he had insight from his Lord. It was with regard to that determination that he could say that Adam and those below him would be under his banner on the Day of Resurrection, and that Moses, were he living, would have to follow him, and that he would be the first to knock upon the gate of Paradise and to open the gate of intercession, together with comparable indications found in transmitted reports.</p>
<p>In fact, many things drawn forth by prayer and supplication from hidden affairs and judgments belong to these concealed matters and states. Apart from them, nothing comes about save what is written, established and allotted in the Presence of knowledge; that cannot be increased or diminished.</p>
<p>Some of those who know God and have stood in the universal Presences call certain considerations of oneness, included at the first rank, “essential affairs” (<em>shuʾūn dhātiyya</em>). At the second and lower ranks these appear as fundamental realities and certain stable attendant qualities, such as life and knowledge, or as stable things such as individual substances and essences, and as the properties of endurance and permanence attached to some of the meanings of “affair”.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p24" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p24"><h3 id="title-b2007-p24">B2007 p. 24 · The first comprehensive determination</h3>

<p>These are among the meanings of <em>shaʾn</em> (“affair,” “concern”). Some call certain of them “essential states” (<em>aḥwāl dhātiyya</em>). They appear as they pass from one form into another, whether intelligible or sensory: contraction and expansion, contentment and anger, and all accidents that do not endure; and likewise thoughts, images, and imaginal and sensory configurations in this world, the intermediate state, and the next. Recall here the transmitted report concerning the Real—exalted and holy—appearing, in the hereafter, in a form in which a people do not recognize Him, and then in a form in which they do recognize Him. God is the Guide.</p>
<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> Know that the first consideration and determination to become determined from the Unseen is this unity from which <em>aḥadiyya</em> and <em>wāḥidiyya</em> arise. It thus remains an intermediary (<em>barzakh</em>) comprehending both. It is like the reality of love, from which being a lover and being beloved arise, while love comprehends both, removes what stands between them, and unifies them.</p>
<p>Or one may say that it is the exigency of the true inwardness expressed by “I was a hidden treasure”: manifestation is what is expressed by “that I might be known.” This first consideration and determination, which is identical with the Essence under the aspect of intermediacy and comprehensiveness just mentioned, is the Essence's own receptivity to its inwardness, its unseen depth, the negation of considerations from it, and the judgment of its pre-eternity; and equally to its manifestation and to the manifestation of the considerations it contains, which affirm its character of everlastingness for itself—first comprehensively, then in detail.</p>
<p>This receptivity is the origin of every receptivity and also of every activity. Although it is identical with the Essence, it is as though the Essence speaks to itself within itself, informing itself concerning the manifestation demanded by its nature, the disclosure of the considerations of its oneness, and the essential perfection—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p25" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p25"><h3 id="title-b2007-p25">B2007 p. 25 · Inward speech, hearing, vision, and the precedence of manifestation</h3>

<p>—and the name-related perfection that pertains to that manifestation: a speaking and informing transcendent of corporeal articulation, through a transcendent, unitary “letter” identical with the Essence and containing every universal and particular meaning, and all the utterances and words, both spoken and enacted, that indicate them, at the seventh and most inward rank of speech.</p>
<p>This is the speech alluded to in the saying attributed to the Prophet: “The Qurʾān has an outward and an inward; within its inward is another inward, down to seven inward depths.” It resembles our speaking within ourselves without the intermediary of an outward letter or audible sound. Within that same receptivity there is also the capacity of the Essence to incline toward that inward discourse through hearing and attentive listening: this inclination is in truth the effect of the original love. It therefore inclines to listen at the seventh, most inward degree of inclination and hearing.</p>
<p>Within that receptivity, too, is the capacity of the Essence to behold the light of its beauty, which is identical with its oneness and its manifestation, and with the manifestation of its considerations, and to regard the perfection that belongs to them in accordance with this inclination, hearing, and attentiveness. Its beholding accordingly occurs at the seventh, most inward degree of contemplation.</p>
<p>There is also the capacity to be affected by this inward discourse in such a way as to remove the veil created by the predominance of the majesty of the Unseen and hiddenness over beauty and manifestation. This removal is figuratively expressed as the precedence and predominance of mercy over what is called anger, considered as the utmost limit of its judgment in an ascending, not descending, direction. In its most inward character this anger is non-manifestation, bearing the meaning of destruction and nonexistence.</p>
<p>For manifestation and non-manifestation were, in the exigency of this first receptivity, of equal standing. Yet the effect of this discourse, love, and the essential inclination caused the judgment of manifestation to predominate over non-manifestation and assigned it priority. Thus the most holy Essence disclosed itself to itself according to that effect, predominance, and precedence; it appeared to itself in itself—that is, precisely in the first determination and first receptivity. Through that self-disclosure, which is itself knowledge and witnessing, the Essence found itself by way of the mirror just mentioned. That mirror is identical with the Essence, bears the disclosure, and contains within itself the inward discourse, inclination, contemplation, and efficacy of that discourse.</p>
<p>That discourse, directed to itself, is identical with the first self-disclosure and receptivity, but bears the consideration of a meaning that is the inward reality of the attributes of speech, hearing, sight, and power at the seventh inward degree of each—namely, the rank of the first determination. For “speech” is an exhalation issuing from within the speaker, containing a meaning whose appearance the speaker seeks; that exhalation becomes differentiated according to the successive points of articulation. In the same way, original love, which is identical with the first determination and receptivity, contains a meaning of perfection related to manifestation and calling for self-disclosure—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p26" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p26"><h3 id="title-b2007-p26">B2007 p. 26 · From undifferentiated meanings to attributes</h3>

<p>—at the first determination, corresponding to the exhalation itself as it issues from the hidden inwardness of the speaker. “Hearing” is the reception of that meaning, whether outwardly or inwardly. “Sight” is receptivity to its appearance through what becomes manifest to its recipient. “Power” is the capacity to bring about what is intended to appear.</p>
<p>It is this meaning that Shaykh Ibn al-Fāriḍ—may God have mercy on him—intended in his verses, in which he says, approximately:</p>
<blockquote>My utterance—and wholly within me I am a tongue that speaks;<br>my glance—and wholly within me I am an eye that contemplates.<br><br>My hearing—wholly I hear the call as I am summoned;<br>and all of me, warding off extinction within me, is a hand of power.<br><br>Meanings of attributes were established beyond the clothing of appearance;<br>and names of the Essence spread what the senses had related.</blockquote>

<p>That is to say, those meanings were established at the first rank, beyond the rank in which they were clothed with the judgments of plurality and distinction while they were still essential affairs. Once clothed in those judgments, the very same meanings became differentiated attributes in the second rank, according to its law—for example, hearing, sight, power, speech, and the like. At the first rank they had not been attributes, but considerations neither differentiated nor mutually other.</p>
<p>Thus the utterance through which the whole Essence is a tongue speaking inwardly to itself; the glance by which all of it is an observing eye so that what is inward may pass into outward appearance; the hearing by which all of it hears its own discourse; and the hand by which all of it acts to repel non-manifestation—figuratively called “destruction” through its association with concealment and inwardness—toward manifestation and existence: all these are the meanings of the attributes of hearing, sight, power, and speech. They are established as distinct in the second rank of divinity, but the inward realities of those attributes were not different at the first rank, which is their seventh inward depth relative to the outermost end of their manifestation.</p>
<p>The outermost appearance of these attributes is their manifestation in the spoken word issuing from the human tongue, seeing through the eye, hearing through the ear, and acting through the hand—all attributed to the form of the body.</p>
<p><strong>Its first inward level:</strong> these attributes are attributed to the person's soul, but insofar as it is distinguished from the souls of other animals only by the outward form of an intellect concerned with ordinary livelihood and restricted to worldly affairs. Thus the person's speaking, hearing, looking, and acting concern only the world and do not extend to the hereafter, which should be their ultimate end. This is the condition described in the Qurʾān: “They know an outward aspect of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter” (30:7).</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p27" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p27"><h3 id="title-b2007-p27">B2007 p. 27 · The seven inward degrees of a human faculty</h3>

<p><strong>Its second inward level:</strong> what is attributed to the soul insofar as its intellect is illumined by the light of revealed law and faith in God, His books, His messengers, and the realities of the hereafter. Through sound understanding, right reason, and firm faith, the person moves in speech, hearing, seeing, and action from what concerns the world to what concerns the hereafter.</p>
<p><strong>Its third inward level:</strong> what is attributed to the person's immaterial spiritual spirit, whose determination and distinction are established in the world of spirits and the Preserved Tablet.</p>
