For producing an effect proceeds only from one who lives, knows a thing in himself, wills its manifestation and has the power to bring it about. Through knowledge and will he issues to the thing, as it were, a command that it appear, and the thing appears. Speech is thus the form taken by the command addressed to a known thing whose existence is willed. In the bringing forth of spirits, <strong>speech is a pillar</strong> and power a completing condition; in the case of bodies the relationship is reversed. Hence the realm of spirits is called the <strong>world of command</strong> (<em>ʿālam al-amr</em>).</p>
<p><strong>Generosity</strong> is a condition for the effect of speech to become manifest when existence is willed: pouring forth existence by choice can occur only through generosity by which existence is granted. These two—speech and generosity—are conditions of the judgment and command of bringing into being, which proceed from the second determination and the rank of Divinity through the Keys permeating the names and appearing as their active character.</p>
<p><strong>Equity</strong> is another condition, but through the Keys permeating the receptive realities and appearing within them as the capacity to receive the judgment and command that bring them into being. Accordingly the divine name <strong>the Originator</strong> assigned within the Tablet to each of the pillars a special manifestation and a spiritual form, although each comprehends the effects of the others.</p>
<p><strong>Isrāfīl</strong> is the manifestation of the pillar of original, universal and comprehensive <strong>life</strong>, containing every perfection and comprehensive awareness of them. Hence everlasting life in the hereafter is connected to his <strong>second blowing in the Trumpet</strong>. The Trumpet is the locus, foundation and gathering point of natural and elemental forms, above and below. His second blast brings creatures to life and causes them to rise, gazing at the shining lights issuing from the Presence of Lordship without intermediaries or causes on the Day of Resurrection.</p>
<p>His <strong>first blast</strong>, by contrast, consists in raising the breath and returning it from outwardness to inwardness so that the judgment of worldly life may come entirely to an end and return to its origin. Then there begins the judgment of—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p77" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p77"><h3 id="title-b2007-p77">B2007 p. 77 · The four angels and the principles they manifest</h3>

<p>—its appearance and its differentiated forms within the <strong>life of the hereafter</strong>. For this reason <strong>Isrāfīl</strong> is the manifestation of life, as we have said. Equity is included within that life because its comprehensive judgment embraces every thing, original and derivative.</p>
<p>As for <strong>Gabriel (Jibrīl)</strong>, he is a manifestation within the Preserved Tablet of the pillar of <strong>knowledge</strong>. Hence he bears revelation, which comprises the kinds and degrees of knowledge, and he is a teacher, as one interpretation of God's saying has it: “One mighty in power taught him” (Qurʾān 53:5). He is also an intermediary in the formation of Jesus, insofar as Jesus is the Word of the Real and a sign of the Hour. Gabriel is thus a manifestation of both knowledge and speech. Inasmuch as he manifests knowledge he is called the <strong>Holy Spirit</strong> (<em>Rūḥ al-Qudus</em>); inasmuch as he manifests speech he is called the <strong>Trustworthy Spirit</strong> (<em>al-Rūḥ al-Amīn</em>).</p>
<p>He therefore possesses two aspects and two judgments, like Isrāfīl, peace be upon them. Under the aspect of his outward reality, in which the judgment of existence predominates, Gabriel manifests speech, for speech is the form of breath, which is identical with existence. Under the aspect of his inward reality, in which the judgment of knowledge predominates, he becomes its manifestation. Pay heed to this noble secret and you will attain the treasuries of gnosis. God is the Guide.</p>
<p>As for <strong>Michael (Mīkāʾīl)</strong>, he manifests the pillar of <strong>will</strong>, for he arranges that by which creation is preserved through spiritual and formal sustenance: knowledge, understanding and nourishment; imagined sustenance, such as honor and social standing; and sensible sustenance, such as wealth and blessings. He manifests will, with generosity included within it, since the continued effect of will depends on generosity.</p>
<p>As for <strong>ʿAzrāʾīl</strong>, he manifests the pillar of <strong>power</strong>. He subdues tyrants and causes them, through death and annihilation, to be brought low without resistance or the possibility of averting him, so perfectly does he realize the form of power.</p>
<p>Just as all the divine and cosmic realities are subordinate to these four foundations, all spirits and angels are subordinate to these <strong>four angels and their powers</strong>, after the Pen and the enraptured spirits. These last are the <strong>Exalted Ones</strong> (<em>al-ʿālūn</em>), who did not enter under the command to prostrate to Adam because they are wholly enraptured in the majesty of the Real's beauty—glorious is His majesty. This is alluded to by “Were you arrogant, or were you among the Exalted Ones?” (Qurʾān 38:75). The branching of other spirits from these angels corresponds to the branching of other intelligible realities from their principles in the Presence of Knowledge.</p>
<p>All that the Preserved Tablet contains of universal and particular spirits, together with the enraptured spirits above them, falls into <strong>three classes</strong>. One is restricted to having <strong>no natural, imaginal or elemental sensory manifestation</strong>. Another is restricted to possessing a manifestation. A third is not restricted either to possession or non-possession of such a manifestation. Among the first are the enraptured spirits. The second divides into two classes: one to which a manifestation is attributed, but which is not attributed to its manifestation. These are the angels of the heavens and earth to whom affairs and effects are attributed as their powers, intended by the divine words—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p78" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p78"><h3 id="title-b2007-p78">B2007 p. 78 · Human spirits and the meaning of angels' wings</h3>

<p>—“Those who race ahead, and those who govern the affair” (Qurʾān 79:4–5); “By those that scatter” (51:1); and “those who distribute the affair” (51:4), and similar verses.</p>
<p>The <strong>second</strong> class among those tied to a manifestation comprises spirits <strong>attributed to their manifestations</strong>, such as human spirits attributed to their individual bodies and temperaments. Every human spirit becomes determined from the Presence of the Preserved Tablet, either from its own reality, from its determinations that are principal realities, or from what branches from these principles or their branches and further branches, indefinitely. Such a spirit is prior to the determination of the individual's elemental temperament.</p>
<p>Only after that temperament has been determined does the relationship of this spirit's manifestation as <strong>governor</strong> become determined. Under that relationship it is called the <strong>soul at peace</strong> (<em>al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinna</em>), breathed into the portion determined from this spirit, which is attributed to the manifestation of the divine Presence. Understand this.</p>
<p>The same applies to the spirituality of every individual, whether mineral, plant or animal. The forms of the jinn, restricted to fiery manifestations, also belong to this class.</p>
<p>The <strong>third main class</strong> comprises spirits neither bound to a manifestation nor bound to its absence. They may appear in whatever manifestation they wish, or without one. They are the messengers and ambassadors between the Real and His creation, intended by God's saying: “Messengers having wings, two, three and four; He increases creation as He wills” (Qurʾān 35:1).</p>
<p>Every one of these spirits necessarily possesses <strong>two powers</strong>, by which they fly in the expanse of the Real's command and nearness. One is a <strong>cognitive power</strong> receiving from the Originator, exalted is He. The second is a <strong>practical power</strong> acting according to that knowledge in order to realize its character in oneself. These two powers are expressed by <strong>the two wings</strong>.</p>
<p>God may give some a <strong>third wing</strong>: teaching to another what He taught them, as in “One mighty in power taught him” (Qurʾān 53:5). He may give some a <strong>fourth wing</strong>: performing an act for the benefit of another by the permission and command of the Lord, as in “They glorify the praise of their Lord, believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe” (Qurʾān 40:7). These four are the universal classes of their powers and wings.</p>
<p>The particular forms referred to by “He increases creation as He wills” (35:1) are without limit. Thus the report that the Prophet, peace be upon him, saw Gabriel with <strong>six hundred wings</strong> is among the ways in which God adds to creation without limit. Reflect on this chapter; you will attain secrets very difficult to obtain. God is the Guide.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" data-part-start="Foundation III · Cosmos and Adam" id="b2007-p79" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p79"><h3 id="title-b2007-p79">B2007 p. 79 · Third foundation: from the Breath to imaginal and corporeal reality</h3>

<p><strong>THIRD FOUNDATION: On the determination of the imaginal world and the rank of bodies, down to the composition of Adam's form, peace be upon him.</strong></p>
<p>Know that the <strong>Breath of the All-merciful</strong> (<em>al-nafas al-raḥmānī</em>), identical with prior mercy embracing every thing outwardly and inwardly, when it appeared from within the true Unseen by the demand of “then I loved,” was identical with the <strong>first determination, disclosure and intermediacy</strong> at the first rank: one, transcendent and comprehensively undifferentiated.</p>
<p>The Keys of the Unseen and oneness, together with the affairs and states they contained—namely, their relations and considerations—were a kind of <strong>relational, not real, differentiation</strong> of that real comprehensiveness. No judgment of otherness or difference arose between what was comprehended and what was differentiated.</p>
<p>This same all-merciful Breath also appeared in a form of <strong>real differentiation in knowledge</strong>, and <strong>relational differentiation in name-related existence</strong>, and in a form of <strong>real comprehensiveness in existence</strong> and <strong>relational comprehensiveness in knowledge</strong>. It appeared from the hiddenness of that first determination, disclosure and intermediacy, from its real comprehensiveness and the relational differentiation included within it, according to the original demand of love at the second rank.</p>
<p>Thus this all-merciful Breath was also identical with the <strong>second determination, self-disclosure and intermediacy</strong>, through and within which divine and cosmic realities and names appeared. Furthermore, from the standpoint of the second determination, the very shadow of this Breath was the totality of the relational differentiation existing at the first rank.</p>
<p>The pillars of this second disclosure, determination and intermediacy, together with their completing conditions, are the <strong>seven principal names and attributes</strong> established at its centre. From them arise divine and cosmic names and attributes within the Cloud-like Presence and at its two extremes, in a multiplicity and differentiation without limit, as genera, species and individuals. All these become the <strong>differentiation of the comprehensive reality</strong>—but a <strong>real</strong> rather than merely relative differentiation.</p>
<p>This comprehensiveness and its differentiation are both intelligible and existential with respect to the Originator who knows them, exalted and holy—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p80" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p80"><h3 id="title-b2007-p80">B2007 p. 80 · Two aspects of the Breath and the emergence of hābāʾ</h3>

<p>—and they are intelligible but not existential relative to the understanding and witnessing of other possible things. The second rank, second determination, second disclosure and intermediacy, with everything they contain comprehensively and in differentiation, are <strong>Unseen and inward</strong> relative to all cosmic ranks and their inhabitants. They are the shadow and image of the first rank and its determination, disclosure and intermediacy. The pillars of the second rank are shadows and manifestations of the Keys of the Unseen; its real differentiation manifests their relational differentiation, as explained.</p>
<p>This all-merciful Breath at the second rank, and insofar as it is <strong>light</strong>, has <strong>two judgments</strong>. First, it <strong>bestows existence through will and choice</strong>. Second, its effect, ray and shadow are <strong>bestowed</strong> by virtue of its willing. As God says, “Had He willed, He would have made it still” (Qurʾān 25:45)—that is, its shadow and ray. Had He not brought any possible thing into existence, He would have remained perfect in His Essence and would have lacked nothing of His perfections.</p>
<p>When He willed, He extended the shadow of His light and the ray of His manifestation through bringing the world into existence, according to the demand of original love, the orientations and conjunctions of the principal names, and the efficacy of the creative command.</p>
<p>An effect or shadow of this all-merciful Breath therefore appeared in the <strong>rank of spirits</strong>, which is more closely related to the Unseen and the Presence of Necessity than the rank of bodies. The latter is more closely related to witnessing and the Presence of Knowledge—or, say, of Possibility. That first effect was the <strong>Supreme Pen</strong> and the spiritual form of its determination. Its existence was a comprehensive totality containing the relational existential differentiations established at the second rank.</p>
<p>Then, from the unseen comprehensiveness of the Pen, an effect of that bestowed Breath appeared, according to the demand of love, the orientations and conjunctions of the names, and the creative command, in the form of the <strong>Preserved Tablet</strong>. It became differentiated through its substance and pillars and through what it contained of words of act and utterance, angelic spiritual forms, and the other spiritual sovereignties of every thing. The pillars of this Tablet, named <strong>Isrāfīl, Gabriel, Michael and ʿAzrāʾīl</strong>, manifest the pillars of the second rank. The existential, spiritual articulations branching from these pillars as words of act and utterance manifest the intelligible differentiation of the second rank.</p>
<p>Thereafter, by virtue of original love, the orientations and conjunctions of the principal divine names, and the orientations of their universal spiritual manifestations, an effect of the bestowed all-merciful Breath appeared <strong>from within the Tablet under its fourth aspect</strong>—the aspect of descent and taking natural and elemental, simple and composite forms.</p>
<p>This further manifestation took the form of <strong>the universal dust or hābāʾ</strong>, a matter receptive to every simple or compound natural and elemental form whatever. This—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p81" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p81"><h3 id="title-b2007-p81">B2007 p. 81 · Four qualities and the imaginal rank as intermediary</h3>

<p>—<strong>hābāʾ</strong> was a comprehensive origin and store containing every individual existence and every indivisible part from which subtle and dense bodies and natural and elemental forms are compounded. It possesses <strong>four simple rather than composite principles</strong>: heat, cold, moisture and dryness.</p>
<p>This dust-like reality, through its comprehensiveness and inclusion of the four simple principles, became the first comprehensive manifestation of the Tablet's fourth aspect. These simple principles themselves became existential manifestations of the intelligible pillars attributed to the second rank: <strong>life, knowledge, will and power</strong>.</p>
<p>Thus innate heat belongs especially among the concomitants of animal life; the perfection of knowledge is described as the <strong>coolness and snow of certainty</strong>; inclination, whose form is flowing, belongs among the concomitants of moisture; and overpowering, belonging to the consequences of power, has in dryness its dryness and hardness. Thus each natural principle manifests a spiritual principle inasmuch as the influence of one prevails over those of the others. The dust-like reality constitutes comprehensively the differentiation of the <em>malakūt</em> of every thing; the forms, substances and indivisible parts included in its pillars articulate what was comprehended.</p>
<p>This dust-like reality is an effect of the all-merciful Breath, as we have said. Yet it combines <strong>unity and simplicity</strong>, attributed to the side of the Presence of Necessity because it manifests the Tablet—which is dominated by that Presence—with <strong>multiplicity and composition</strong>, special to the Presence of Possibility or Knowledge, because orientations toward descent multiply and it receives manifestation in the clearest, most subtle forms of composition.</p>
<p>Because it combines these two judgments, it has a connection and affinity with the <strong>Cloud-like Presence</strong>. Its first locus of realization was a portion of that Presence equally related to Necessity and Possibility. This portion is called the <strong>rank of image and differentiated imagination</strong> (<em>martabat al-mithāl wa-l-khayāl al-munfaṣil</em>). It is equally related to the unseen of the world of spirits, the locus of simple forms, and to the witnessed realm of sense, the locus of composite forms.</p>
<p>Life and knowledge are dominated by the judgment of unity and comprehensive inclusion, since their actuality does not depend on multiplicity and differentiation. Will and power, however, are dominated by multiplicity and differentiation, since their determinations depend upon distinction and efficacy, both of which signify plurality.</p>
<p>Consequently <strong>acting</strong> is attributed to the manifestations of life and knowledge among the principles of hābāʾ—<strong>heat and cold</strong>—while <strong>being affected</strong> is specifically attributed to those of will and power—<strong>moisture</strong>—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p82" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p82"><h3 id="title-b2007-p82">B2007 p. 82 · Nature, spherical form, and three dimensions</h3>

<p>—and <strong>dryness</strong>. Through the appearance of the mixing of the effects of original love permeating these qualities, a subtle, light blending occurred among them; <strong>nature</strong> (<em>al-ṭabīʿa</em>) is the name of what resulted from that blending. Nature became an intermediary gathering the four principles.</p>
<p>By the demand of love and the orientations of the names and their spiritual manifestations toward the perfection of disclosure, nature became fully and uniformly extended under the judgment of its locus, the <strong>imaginal world</strong>. In that extension it took the form nearest to unity and simplicity, namely <strong>roundness</strong>. The name <strong>the Originator</strong> assigned that spherical form to extended nature, and it became one, relatively simple <strong>Throne</strong>, circular and surrounding the entire world of forms and created dominion.</p>
<p>Because this dust-like reality manifests the fourth aspect of the Tablet, and that aspect has three judgments especially belonging to it, the following were realized. <strong>First</strong>, the judgment of descent into the lowest sensory rank and its composite forms, through which <strong>length</strong> necessarily belongs to body. <strong>Second</strong>, the judgment of differentiation and formal composition, through which <strong>breadth</strong> appears in it. <strong>Third</strong>, the judgment of governance preserving those descending differentiated and compounded forms, through another effect from their source lying inwardly within them, through which <strong>depth</strong> is realized in body.</p>
<p>For this reason some people of unveiling saw the Throne's form as a <strong>triangle</strong>. Others saw it as a <strong>square</strong>, because its determination proceeded from the four natural principles. As it arises from these four principles in the three meanings just mentioned, the Throne's form was divided into <strong>twelve divisions</strong>, which are conceptual rather than sensible.</p>
<p>Because this dust-like reality is the manifestation of the Tablet's fourth aspect, whose judgment descends into the lowest degrees of plurality and composition, the judgment of composition and the collectivity obtained from its principles, peculiar to body, was established inwardly within this Throne-form. The reality of this Throne-configuration, according to the rank where it appeared, was thus <strong>imaginal</strong>.</p>
<p>Then the Originator determined for it another circular configuration according to the judgment of descent into the farthest degrees of multiplicity and composition and its effect within the dust-like reality. This <strong>corporeal configuration</strong> is called <strong>the Throne</strong>, insofar as it is the sphere of spheres, the unstarred sphere, the zodiacal sphere and the rotating sphere.</p>
<p>The three judgments of <strong>length, breadth and depth</strong> belong to this second and derivative configuration. Under this attribution it is the reality of the <strong>Universal Body</strong>. Thus this—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p83" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p83"><h3 id="title-b2007-p83">B2007 p. 83 · Five meanings of istiwāʾ and the Throne</h3>

<p>—<strong>Throne</strong> is so named insofar as its determination and realization occur within a portion of the Cloud-like Presence, as explained. That Presence is the place of establishment of the Lord whose judgment of Lordship comprehends all creatures, an attribution particular to the name <strong>al-Raḥmān</strong>, as is reported in the authentic transmitted account. Hence this Throne is the place of establishment of al-Raḥmān under <em>all the meanings of istiwāʾ</em>.</p>
<p>The first is <strong>settling and becoming established</strong>, as when one says that someone settled upon his mount. The second is <strong>taking control</strong>, as in the saying that someone gained mastery over Iraq. The third is <strong>completion and attaining the utmost degree</strong>, as when one says a man attained the full measure of his youth. The fourth is <strong>intending and directing oneself toward</strong>, as in “Then He turned to the heaven” (Qurʾān 2:29), meaning that He intended and directed Himself toward creating it. The fifth is <strong>equilibrium</strong>, as when one says a thing became even or balanced.</p>
<p>Thus “The All-merciful established Himself upon the Throne” (Qurʾān 20:5) means that the command of existence became established through the capacity to bring into being the genera and kinds of the world's forms, because their substances and material for formation became determined within this dust-like reality.</p>
<p>Through it He took mastery over every rank of His kingdom contained therein, composing its substances however He willed and giving its material whatever form He wished, whenever He wished and for as long as He wished. This Throne is the origin of the determination of <strong>forms of time</strong> through its circular motion.</p>
<p>Thus the command of existence attained its full manifestation in respect of the principles of its ranks: <strong>meaning, spirit, form, and the origins of time and place</strong>. It reached its limit with respect to those principles, turned and directed itself toward the composition of substances and the articulation of forms, and maintained an equilibrium between complete manifestation and complete hiddenness, and between comprehensive inclusion and differentiation.</p>
<p>Just as the second determination and disclosure was the first <strong>comprehensive intelligible divine manifestation</strong> of the original all-merciful Breath through the demand of love and the orientation of the divine Keys, and the pillars and original principles of the second disclosure with their derivatives were its first <strong>differentiated intelligible manifestation</strong>, so the Supreme Pen became the second <strong>comprehensive spiritual cosmic manifestation</strong> of that Breath and the Preserved Tablet its <strong>differentiated spiritual cosmic manifestation</strong>.</p>
<p>The Pen is more closely related to the first disclosure, and the Tablet to the second determination and disclosure. Likewise, when the dust-like reality was determined, the <strong>comprehensive imaginal configuration of the Throne</strong>, together with the comprehensive corporeal configuration included within it, became determined—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p84" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p84"><h3 id="title-b2007-p84">B2007 p. 84 · Three aspects of the Footstool and the emergence of time</h3>

<p>—and its relation as a manifestation of the <strong>Pen</strong> was therefore stronger. The reality of love, through the orientations and conjunctions of the names and their spiritual manifestations, then required that from this dust-like reality and its principles a <strong>natural form receptive to differentiation</strong> be determined, to become the manifestation and natural image of the Preserved Tablet and its articulation, with a stronger relationship to it.</p>
<p>The name <strong>the Originator</strong> assigned it a <strong>spherical form</strong>, a receptive manifestation within which the differentiated details of intelligible, spiritual and sensory forms, subtle and dense, could appear. This is called the <strong>noble Footstool</strong> (<em>al-Kursī al-Karīm</em>).</p>
<p>By the judgment of the <strong>threefold character of its intermediaries</strong>, this noble Footstool possesses <strong>three aspects</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>First:</strong> insofar as the judgment of comprehensive inclusion, unity and simplicity appears within it, the Footstool borders on a portion and judgment of the Presence of Necessity, one of the two aspects of the Cloud-like Presence. This portion is called the <strong>rank of spirits</strong>. That aspect of the Footstool becomes a <strong>mirror</strong> for the manifestation of every spiritual form, which takes an imaginal shape within it denser than its spiritual configuration but subtler than a compounded elemental bodily form.</p>
<p><strong>Second:</strong> insofar as the judgment of differentiated detail, composition and plurality from the natural principles appears within it, the Footstool borders on a portion of the Presence of Possibility, the other aspect of the Cloud-like Presence. This portion is called the <strong>rank of sensation and witnessing</strong>. This aspect of the Footstool becomes a receptive mirror for every compounded elemental form, and for the actions, words, states, accidents and qualities arising from it. Their forms here are subtler than those they have in the sensory world, and become determined within this mirror only <strong>after</strong> the corresponding forms are determined in the sensory world.</p>
<p>Within its imaginal form under this second aspect, the Footstool possesses a corporeal configuration, as was described of the Throne. Under this corporeal aspect the Footstool is called the <strong>sphere of stars and celestial stations</strong>.</p>
<p>Because the Throne and Footstool both possess these judgments, <strong>circular motion</strong> is attributed to them. From that motion, taking place in relation to the Throne-configuration from a point and centre within the Footstool-configuration, the <strong>daily measure of time</strong> becomes determined; through the motion itself, the reality of <strong>time</strong> becomes determined.</p>
<p><strong>Third:</strong> the aspect comprehending the first two and bearing their most subtle judgments. It borders on its own world and its very rank, a portion of the Cloud-like Presence which is the precise <strong>intermediacy between Necessity and Possibility</strong> at the second determination—</p>

</section><section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p85" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p85"><h3 id="title-b2007-p85">B2007 p. 85 · The Footstool and the three paradisal Gardens</h3>

<p>It borders upon the world of the Unseen and meanings, but under the differentiation of that intermediacy, not its comprehensive inclusion. This noble Footstool is the origin of the Gardens. Its three aspects are the principles of their ranks: the Garden of Works, the Garden of Inheritance, and the Garden of Gracious Bestowal. Their degrees are images and manifestations of the principles of the ninety-nine divine names, whose number is completed to a hundred by the name <strong>Allāh</strong>, comprehending them all. The transmitted report states that Paradise contains a hundred degrees, the distance between each like the distance between heaven and earth; the highest is Firdaws, from which four rivers spring, and above which is the Throne. When asking God, one should ask for Firdaws.</p>
<p>The four rivers refer to the four natural principles. From heat flows the river of wine; from cold, the river of water; from moisture, the river of milk; and from dryness, the river of honey, after their mutual compositions. The near ones drink from them unmixed; the righteous believers drink them mixed and composed.</p>
<p>Within the Footstool's comprehensive aspect all spiritual realities destined to manifest in the sensible, compounded realm had already appeared, and through the material of nature and the imaginal world's condition acquired an imaginal form. In this respect Muslim and unbeliever, indeed human and nonhuman, were alike in having their spiritual realities figured there. The Muslim and the unbeliever alike therefore had a dwelling in it when their existential matter and spirituality descended. Hell, meanwhile, was determined beneath the Footstool as a corporeal form related to whatever descended.</p>
<p>When the seven heavens, earth and the realm between them became distinct, the existential matter and spiritual configuration of believer and unbeliever descended until each appeared in a defined sensible form in one of those places. Thus each had a dwelling in Paradise from the aspect of the Footstool just explained, and in Hell from the other aspect. If an unbeliever dies and his spirit does not ascend from Hell to the Garden, because the dense composition of his form and the corporeal judgment prevailing over his spirituality prevent it, his paradisal dwelling remains unused. It is inherited by someone whose spirit ascends from Hell to Paradise through the prevalence of spirituality over nature, and whose relation to the former possessor involves a praiseworthy characteristic or participation under the—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p86" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p86"><h3 id="title-b2007-p86">B2007 p. 86 · Inheritance, vision, command and prohibition</h3>

<p>—scope of a divine name. This aspect of the Footstool is called <strong>Firdaws</strong>, the highest Garden, at one of its two sides, and is the Garden of Inheritance. The comprehending aspect between the two is the <strong>Garden of Gracious Bestowal</strong>, which contains the mound of Vision, the locus of seeing and witnessing, and which is also called the Garden of Eden. The Garden of Works belongs to its lower side, neighboring sensation and witnessed reality.</p>
<p>The one divine command expressed as “Our command is only one” descends according to “He inspired into every heaven its command” (Qurʾān 41:12). To establish and preserve the judgment of unity, it appears in the Throne according to that rank as one. In the Footstool, however, because differentiation and multiplicity have appeared, it divides into <strong>command and prohibition</strong>. Command preserves unity's influence in descent toward multiplicity; prohibition induces the observance of unity through return and ascent from multiplicity to unity.</p>
<p>Since the affair of the two worlds is built on descent and ascent; these are traced to the two principles of unity and multiplicity; and their intended purpose is maintained through command and prohibition, the two were designated figuratively as <strong>the two feet</strong> by which a person stands. Hence the saying that the Footstool is the place of the two feet. This noble Footstool is the seat of the name <strong>al-Raḥīm</strong>, as the Throne, which determines time, manifests the name <strong>al-Dahr</strong> and is the seat of <strong>al-Raḥmān</strong>. Know this; God is the One whose help is sought.</p>
<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> The effect of the all-merciful Breath appeared as universal dust (<em>habāʾ</em>), capable of taking subtle, simple sensible forms that admit no separation, fragmentation, rupture or reunion, as well as denser compounded sensible forms that admit division, composition and corruption. The locus of the former simple, subtle forms, either comprehensively or in detail, was a portion of the Cloud-like Presence called the <strong>imaginal world</strong>.</p>
<p>The resulting forms first appeared there comprehensively as the Throne and the sphere of spheres, constellations, unstarred sphere and limiting sphere; in detail they appeared as the Footstool and the sphere of the celestial stations. Their comprehensiveness was the comprehensiveness of the Tablet's differentiation, and their detail articulated that comprehensiveness. With the imaginal world filled by these forms, there remained of the primordial dust what could receive density, composition and dense compound forms capable of partition under the mixing of its principles and their interpenetration.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p87" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p87"><h3 id="title-b2007-p87">B2007 p. 87 · The first undifferentiated cosmic matter</h3>

<p>The natural principles enter into one another and comprise one another. This composition and mixing arose from the original exigency of love, the orientations and conjunctions of the divine names, and their intelligible, spiritual and imaginal manifestations in the primordial dust and its principles. It took place on the side of the Presence of Possibility called the realm of sensible visibility, for which the shadow of time is in one respect a form and manifestation.</p>
<p>Within that rank the distinctions between the natural principles and their properties were obliterated, so that what had been multiple, distinguishable and detailed at the imaginal rank became <strong>one undifferentiated thing</strong> in the sensible rank. Its comprehensiveness thus corresponded to the detail established in the imaginal rank.</p>
<p>The Qurʾān expresses this composition and mixing as <strong>ratq</strong>, a joining or closing together: “Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and earth were joined, then We split them apart? We made every living thing from water” (21:30). Some call this joined matter the <strong>Supreme Element</strong>, others the <strong>Element of Elements</strong>. It has four principles: fire, air, water and earth, just as primordial dust, its origin, has four principles belonging to nature.</p>
<p>The supreme element and its constituents moved through the original loving impulse pervading them, inseparable from the all-merciful Breath of which that matter is one effect and manifestation. This movement inclined longingly toward the perfection pertaining to its forms and differentiation. Through that movement and yearning an influence [the printed word here is obscure] arose, strong enough to bring out a latent effect of heat.</p>
<p>The subtler portion of the joined matter rose up as <strong>vapor or smoke</strong>, still comprehensive and described through unity: this was the closed state of the heavens. The four principles then became differentiated and the joined condition was opened. Under the quaternary secret descending from the origin and present within every comprehensive rank, they separated into four portions, each dominated by two principles while containing the remaining two. The densest, dominated by cold and dryness, became earth, the joined state of the terrestrial realm. The next, subtler portion, dominated by cold and moisture, became water.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p88" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p88"><h3 id="title-b2007-p88">B2007 p. 88 · Elements and the program of celestial manifestations</h3>

<p>The third and subtler portion was dominated by heat and moisture, with the remaining principles still present: it became air. The fourth, subtler still, was dominated by heat and dryness while containing the others: it became fire.</p>
<p>The names <strong>Allāh</strong> and <strong>al-Raḥmān</strong>, being directed toward realization of the perfection belonging to their subordinate divine names, realities and effects, were likewise directed to the manifestation of that perfection. Yet this depends upon the appearance of the judgments of cosmic realities that serve as loci of the divine names' effects. Their purpose is based on the existential command, whose governing structure consists in the seven original divine names, their orientations and conjunctions.</p>
<p>These occur first through <strong>intelligible manifestations</strong> determined by the Willing; second through <strong>spiritual manifestations</strong> determined by the Originator; third through <strong>imaginal manifestations</strong> consisting in the natural principles and the three corporeal determinations in comprehension and detail, also determined by the Originator; fourth through the <strong>sensory and corporeal manifestations</strong>.</p>
<p>Making name-related perfection appear in detail at every rank depends on the prior determination of manifestations of these principles so that their orientations and conjunctions can take effect. In primordial dust, what was receptive to bodily forms had already been determined; the material prepared for subtle heavenly forms had risen as a joined, subtle smoke, distinct from what was receptive to earthly forms and the other principles.</p>
<p>The command therefore issued from the names <strong>Allāh</strong> and <strong>al-Raḥmān</strong> to <strong>the Fashioner</strong> (<em>al-Muṣawwir</em>) to assign elevated, subtle, corporeal heavenly manifestations and celestial spheres to the seven foundational realities determining the principal names. To those names themselves it assigned luminous <strong>planetary</strong> forms whose orientations, conjunctions, configurations and connections could influence what lay below them in the world of generation and corruption, so that dense terrestrial compound forms—genera, species and individuals of generated beings—might come about.</p>
<p>When the joined matter of the heavens and earth had differentiated into subtle smoke and dense terrestrial composition, the Fashioner assigned each a suitable form. Their matter was addressed: “Come willingly or unwillingly” (Qurʾān 41:11)—that is, receive the form appointed by the Fashioner, willingly in respect of your particular existent mode that recognizes its welfare and perfection in whatever issues—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p89" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p89"><h3 id="title-b2007-p89">B2007 p. 89 · Willing or compelled reception; seven heavens and planets</h3>

<p>—from its universal principle and chooses its reception without resistance; or unwillingly in respect of your possibility and nonexistence, which are ignorant of their welfare and perfection and receive by compulsion in order that the original perfection appear. Both said, “We come willingly,” because they were near the primordial disposition and because the judgment of unity and comprehensiveness, special to existence, predominated over differentiation and multiplicity, the characteristics of possibility.</p>
<p>Under the original motion of love, the orientations and conjunctions of divine names, and the Fashioner's judgment, the spiritual, joined material established in the sensory rank then moved circularly from its center. It acquired the form of a heaven <strong>first from one consideration and fourth from another</strong>. It manifested the attribute of life and the predominance of heat. The Fashioner assigned to the divine name manifested through it—again, the Living—a luminous manifestation, the star called the <strong>Sun</strong>, like the governing soul of that heavenly form.</p>
<p>Above that heaven the Fashioner determined three further heavens, and three below it. Each was assigned a soul to govern it: a heavenly body particular to the heaven, manifesting a divine name determined by the reality of which that heaven itself was a manifestation.</p>
<p>Thus the <strong>fourth heaven</strong>, central among seven, manifested life; the <strong>third</strong>, will; the <strong>second</strong>, equity and justice; and the <strong>first</strong>, speech. The first is therefore particularly related to the <em>Bayt al-ʿIzza</em>, the dwelling of the Qurʾān in its comprehensive descent. The <strong>fifth</strong> manifests power; the <strong>sixth</strong>, knowledge; the <strong>seventh</strong>, generosity. Abraham, characterized by generosity, liberality and fulfilling the duties of hospitality with person, possessions and offspring, was therefore seen in the seventh heaven.</p>
<p>The Sun manifests the name <strong>the Living</strong>, and the supremacy of its dependent name the Life-giver appears especially fully through it. Venus manifests <strong>the Willing</strong>, with its dependent Fashioner's influence predominant. Mercury manifests <strong>the Equitable</strong>, with the effect of the Originator more evident. The Moon manifests <strong>the Speaking</strong>, with its dependent Creator more powerful. Mars manifests <strong>the Powerful</strong>, with the Overpowering especially evident. Jupiter manifests <strong>the Knowing</strong>, and the Wise is most conspicuous through it. Saturn manifests <strong>the Generous</strong>, with the name <strong>Lord</strong> especially powerful in it.</p>
<p>The configurations of the spheres, the forms arising from relations among their parts—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p90" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p90"><h3 id="title-b2007-p90">B2007 p. 90 · Celestial configurations and what really causes effects</h3>

<p>—and the configurations of the planetary connections and conjunctions, including conjunction, opposition, trine, sextile and similar configurations, arise through the motions of those planets in their spheres. Farghānī takes the outward sense of “Each swims in an orbit” (Qurʾān 36:40) as an allusion to this scheme.</p>
<p>These configurations manifest the judgments and effects of divine names and of their dependents, branches and further branches. The principal and derivative names continually manifest effects in the realm of generation and corruption between heaven and earth, at times <strong>through</strong> these celestial causes and manifestations. In this case, the celestial things are <strong>preparations for receiving the names' effects</strong> in the things to which effects come, and not themselves the agents to whom action and efficacy are attributed. Action and efficacy are attributed rather to the <strong>realities of the divine names</strong>.</p>
<p>This is the arrangement proper to the <strong>world of wisdom</strong>, in which power is included and acts through visible means, as with the other causes perceived in the sensory world. At other times the names act through their own realities <strong>without such mediating manifestations</strong>, and in a way contrary to what the outward judgments of visible causes would ordinarily entail. This is the arrangement proper to the <strong>world of power</strong>, in which wisdom is included.</p>
<p>Hence in the sensible life of this world the genera, species and individuals of generated compound forms appear usually through these causes and sometimes without them. In this way name-related perfection concerned with the completion of disclosure becomes manifest: universals through the universal names and effects of their universal manifestations, and particulars through particulars, according to “Say: Each acts according to its own disposition” (Qurʾān 17:84).</p>
<p>All this occurs through the efficacy of the one, comprehensive divine command pervading the realities of these names and their celestial and planetary manifestations, as alluded to by “He inspired into every heaven its command” (41:12)—that is, the command special to each and colored by its judgment.</p>
<p>Differences among the original and derivative divine names and attributes in breadth, comprehensiveness, universality and particularity are reflected in the things branching from each. Following the opening of the heavens and principles, and under the same primordial movement of love and the divine names' orientations and conjunctions through their spiritual, imaginal and sensory manifestations, the previously joined earthly matter stirred. It opened and became earth. The Fashioner gave it a <strong>spherical form under rational apprehension</strong>, while it appeared <strong>flat to ordinary perception</strong>. Farghānī refers to “The earth He spread thereafter” (Qurʾān 79:30).</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p91" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p91"><h3 id="title-b2007-p91">B2007 p. 91 · Time as the measure and condition of movement</h3>

<p>Through the motion attributed to the Throne's form in its twenty-four degrees, the measure generally recognized as an ordinary <strong>day</strong> was established. Through the motion of the Footstool's form, named the sphere of celestial stations and planets, and the determination of the remaining spheres, elements and spread-out earth, the daily revolution of the Throne was divided into night and day, weeks, months and years, together with the sciences for calculating them. All this occurs by the determination of the Mighty, the Knowing.</p>
<p><strong>Time</strong>, the measure of the universal and determinate daily motion, becomes the container and locus for the appearance of all the bodies and accidents comprised within the limiting sphere. These therefore fall under its judgment. For, as already explained, anything inhabiting an intelligible or formal locus falls under that locus's condition and can appear only according to it. Accordingly, time may be regarded as a manifestation and form of the <strong>sensory rank</strong>, which governs every sensible thing by making it appear in conformity to its law. The Creator determines this, and the Fashioner gives it form.</p>
<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> The earlier exposition has shown that the first thing to become determined and manifest from the Unseen of the Unseen was the <strong>divine all-merciful Breath</strong>, unified, including within itself the judgments of activity and efficacy, receptivity and being affected—indeed all names, attributes and acts. The Knower, knowledge, known, agent, receiver and act were then one thing, without differentiation or otherness, at the first rank, which is identical with real unity.</p>
<p>The very same Breath appeared from that Presence and its inwardness at the <strong>second rank</strong>. This is a consideration and determination of the same reality containing, under the aspect of oneness, indefinitely many considerations related to its everlastingness. The first reality or Presence to become differentiated within that second rank was the Presence of <strong>existence</strong>, designated also as the Presence of <strong>Necessity</strong> through a concomitant judgment.</p>
<p><strong>Real unity and relational multiplicity</strong> are attributed to this Presence. Because of its real unity it and its manifestations belong especially to action and efficacy. All the divine names are attributed to it. Opposite it, within the second rank, became differentiated the Presence of <strong>knowledge related to possible things known</strong>, called the Presence of Possibility after what characterizes its contents.</p>
<p>To that Presence, as containing possible realities, are attributed <strong>real multiplicity and a collected relational unity</strong>. Because multiplicity has so strong an affinity to it, the realities belonging to it are characterized by reception, being affected and undergoing change. Yet within the Presence—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p92" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p92"><h3 id="title-b2007-p92">B2007 p. 92 · Necessity and Possibility as the two hands</h3>

<p>—of Necessity, because of the relational multiplicity, there is also a kind of reception: the reception associated with the request of preparedness, supplication, and answering what is asked. And within the Presence of things known and Possible things, because of its relational unity, there is efficacy and activity through requesting and supplicating the Presence of Necessity that is addressed.</p>
<p>The <strong>comprehensive human intermediary</strong>, and the <strong>differentiated Cloud-like intermediary</strong>, both join the two and separate them in differing respects. They include divine attributes and cosmic realities and bear the very existential self-disclosure encompassing them all. <strong>Necessity</strong> is thus one of His hands extended in mercy. Given the particular assignment of that mercy in “Write for us good in this world and in the next ... My mercy encompasses all things, and I shall prescribe it for those who are Godwary, give alms, and believe in Our signs” (Qurʾān 7:156), this is <strong>the right hand</strong>, in relation to their receptivities.</p>
<p>The Presence of known things and Possibility is His other hand. Since the blessing of all name-related perfections in their inward identity and outward manifestation concerns both Presences, <strong>both of His hands are blessed right hands</strong> from the standpoint of true, not merely relative, perfection.</p>
<p>Among spiritual and corporeal manifestations, whatever more strongly displays unity, simplicity and subtlety—such as the heavens—is more closely related to manifestation of the Presence of Necessity, its efficacy and action, and is appropriately attributed to the right hand. Whatever more clearly displays multiplicity, composition and density—such as the earth—more fully manifests the Presence of known and possible things, its reception and being affected, and is more fittingly attributed, with reverence, to the hand without further qualification. Farghānī refers to “The whole earth shall be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens folded in His right hand” (Qurʾān 39:67).</p>
<p>This warns against attributing hand, activity and independent existence to another than God. The <strong>fingers</strong>, if one grasps their meaning, are knowing, willing, power, generosity as excellence in fashioning, and equitable ordering. The Living is like the grasp and the hand; their manifestations appear wherever the command descends.</p>
<p>Where simplicity, unity and subtlety are more evident, the equity and comprehensiveness of the intermediary, pervading all created things, are more hidden because the manifestation is akin to the Presence of Necessity. Where composition, gathering and multiplicity are more evident, the intermediary's equity and comprehensiveness are more apparent, because of a stronger relation to Possibility and known things and because of their effect in uniting differences and gathering disparate realities.</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p93" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p93"><h3 id="title-b2007-p93">B2007 p. 93 · Generation of minerals from the four principles</h3>

<p>Now that this has become clear, know that when the effect of the all-merciful Breath appeared in the form of the <strong>Supreme Element</strong> under a suitable determination of its intermediary character, and the union of its subtler, simple aspect was opened into the seven divisions already described, its denser, compounded aspect was likewise divided into seven. Four are the elements, and three their compound derivatives, completing them as already indicated in our treatment of the original principles. The three derivatives here are the temperaments composed of the elements, namely the three generated kingdoms: <strong>mineral, plant and animal</strong>.</p>
<p>Nothing appears except in a locus and rank receptive to its existence. Accordingly, from the Presence of the name <strong>the Equitable</strong> three ranks of balanced proportion were determined within the Cloud-like intermediary Presence. Each temperament produced through composition of the elements appears in one such rank, and its existence conforms to that rank and its judgment, as in the case of the inhabitants of every rank.</p>
<p>The basis and material of every elemental temperament is a portion of one particular element. Portions drawn from the other elements come upon that fundamental portion through the permeation of original love within the element and its principles, so that the perfection proper to composition may appear.</p>
<p>First was determined the rank of <strong>mineral equilibrium</strong>. Mineral things most closely resemble their elemental mothers: they are stable, possess relatively few powers, require less protection against dissolution, and are less exposed than the later generations to change and corruption. Their primary portion is <strong>fire</strong>, in view of fire's closeness to simple principles and the strength of simplicity within it. Air, water and earth join it, and mixture and composition arise. The composite receives a mineral form from the Presence of the <strong>Fashioner</strong> and an effect from the <strong>Living</strong> which prevents its composition from dissolving and brings it to its proper perfection.</p>
<p>At the first level of the mineral form, its completion requires considerable work and treatment, as with silver and iron. At the intermediate level it needs less treatment, as with gold. At the highest it needs none, as with gems, rubies and coral. Before the other elements join this fiery portion, fiery portions may also combine with it and acquire fiery configurations and temperaments in the mineral rank. <strong>Jinn-spirits</strong> become attached to them and remain concealed from beings whose forms are composed of another kind. Iblīs is the principle of these jinn. They divide into two classes: some are dominated by dark, smoky parts of fire and become rebellious; others are dominated—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p94" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p94"><h3 id="title-b2007-p94">B2007 p. 94 · Mineral perfections and the vegetal and animal kingdoms</h3>

<p>—by the luminous quality of fire and therefore receive the light of faith. The highest mineral grade is capable of receiving a gold-like form on account of its stability and freedom from destruction through fracture, melting, duration and other deficiencies. The mineral generation accordingly possesses properties and benefits absent from the elemental mothers: color, taste, pleasure, strengthening, nourishment, adornment, and use as a means for attaining needs, either directly or indirectly. Because the earthen portion dominates the rest, the mineral is cast down like the earth.</p>
<p>The divine command then descended through the primordial movement of love permeating the element and its principles toward composition. The rank of <strong>vegetal equilibrium</strong> was determined, with air as the primary portion of what is composed there and the remaining elements entering into it. The composite received vegetal form and sought a vegetal spirit from the name <strong>the Living</strong>, by which its form could live and be sustained until the appropriate perfection was attained through the permeation of original love.</p>
<p>Its vegetal spirit introduced powers absent from the elements and mineral forms: <strong>nutrition, growth, reproduction, attraction, repulsion, digestion and retention</strong>. This temperament has three degrees. Lowest are grasses and trees whose benefit, as ordinarily perceived by people, is relatively slight. The middle gives products whose usefulness is widespread and abundant through fruits and other benefits of taste, scent, medicine and the like. The highest adds to mineral and vegetal benefits a resemblance to the animal in many properties and judgments, as in the date palm.</p>
<p>Then the command descended through original love toward further composition. The rank of <strong>animal equilibrium</strong> was determined, and the primary portion of its temperament was <strong>water</strong>: “We made every living thing from water” (Qurʾān 21:30). The other elements entered into that water. The composite received from the Fashioner the form of an animal, a form oriented horizontally, and sought from the Living Self-subsisting an <strong>animal spirit</strong> governing, caring for and preserving it by its powers, whose roots are appetite and anger.</p>
<p>Above what is found in plants, the animal possesses <strong>external senses and voluntary locomotion</strong> from one place to another. In some animals, the predominance of earth draws them to the ground while water carries them into movement; such a creature—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p95" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p95"><h3 id="title-b2007-p95">B2007 p. 95 · Locomotion, comprehensive equilibrium and the human form</h3>

<p>—moves upon its belly in accordance with those two judgments. In another, earth and water predominate in standing and movement, so that it moves upon two legs, as the human being. In a bird the judgments of water and air predominate, so it moves on its feet and flies with its wings. In yet others, the four elements equally contribute to standing and motion, and the animal moves on four legs. Others stand upon more limbs because more numerous elemental and generated powers participate in their constitution. The Qurʾān mentions the three more common groups: creatures moving on their bellies, on two legs or on four, while God creates what He wills (24:45).</p>
<p>The final limit of the divine command's descent and of the bestowed influence of the all-merciful Breath is the <strong>earthen element</strong> and the constitution in which earth is fundamental while the remaining elements join it. That composite contains all the earlier ranks of temperament, because the command has traversed them and been colored by their judgments.</p>
<p>As we have repeatedly explained, the command is <strong>circular</strong>. Its end is joined to its beginning, or indeed is identical with it under a different consideration. At that final terrestrial limit, therefore, a rank of equilibrium was determined comprehending all three earlier equilibria, and indeed both the higher and lower intermediary ranks. This comprehensive rank is an <strong>intelligible image of the first and second intermediaries</strong>, the inmost aspects of human reality, and the measure, origin and source of the various balanced intermediate ranks.</p>
<p>The fully balanced, compounded <strong>human temperament</strong> is also its image, but a sensible image. The divine spirit breathed into it through divine breathing is the image of the outward existential self-disclosure of the divine all-merciful Breath.</p>
<p>Just as the second intermediary, which gathers existence and knowledge of possible things, divine names and attributes, and divine and cosmic realities, is the true image of the first intermediary which comprehends <em>wāḥidiyya</em> and essential <em>aḥadiyya</em>, while the second outward existential disclosure is an image and shadow of the first inward, hidden disclosure, so the comprehensive rank of human equilibrium and the human compound formed within it after the spirit was breathed into it became an image of the intermediacy and disclosure with all their outward and inward names, realities and attributes. Farghānī then cites the reported saying that God created Adam in His image, or in the—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p96" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p96"><h3 id="title-b2007-p96">B2007 p. 96 · Adam and Muḥammad: two kinds of comprehensiveness</h3>

<p>—image of <strong>al-Raḥmān</strong>. Thus Adam, in his reality, comprehends all that the second intermediary and disclosure comprehend of divine and cosmic names, attributes and realities. Muḥammad—God bless him and grant him peace—by his reality and form comprehends all that the <strong>first intermediary</strong> comprehends of the Keys, the One and the One-in-Unicity, with a truly unitary comprehensiveness in which no judgment predominates over any other.</p>
<p>Just as angels are among the powers of the hand attributed to the all-merciful image in which Adam was created—indeed manifestations of that form—they are likewise manifestations of the properties of Adam's reality and components of his comprehensive form. Adam's reality and image constitute their whole.</p>
<p>The perfection of a whole becomes manifest in two ways. First, through its universality and the comprehensive gathering of its parts, even if each individual part remains deficient. Second, through making each individual part perfect by removing its deficiency, so that the perfection of the whole becomes manifest through the perfection of its parts and not merely through its collectivity. It may also appear through both.</p>
<p>The Real therefore willed to perfect Adam, and whomever He chose among his exceptional descendants, <strong>from both aspects</strong>. He began by perfecting the components. The opening of that perfection was God's address to the angels, the noblest parts of Adam among created beings, in the manner of consultation: “I am placing a vicegerent on earth” (Qurʾān 2:30). This was in order that the imperfections latent in them through their <strong>possibility and created nature</strong> should be made manifest.</p>
<p>Among these were their criticisms of Adam and the imputation to him of violent wrongdoing and bloodshed without observing any such act issuing from him; imputing a grave offense without proof; testifying before being summoned; harboring ill opinion; searching out faults; voicing them; reasoning from the instruments of appetite and anger to the conclusion that Adam would corrupt and shed blood; neglecting certainty and direct inspection; speaking against Adam in the divine Presence; envy of his virtue and suitability for vicegerency; eagerness for the rank of vicegerent; and the mistaken assumption that they themselves were qualified, even though this rested on an apparent ground.</p>
<p>That ground was their possession of comprehensiveness under three aspects: the <strong>Reality of Realities</strong>, comprehending perfections—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p97" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p97"><h3 id="title-b2007-p97">B2007 p. 97 · The deficiency of angelic understanding and the conditions of vicegerency</h3>

<p>—pervading all parts by its universality; <strong>universal unconditioned existence</strong>, comprehending names and their perfections; and <strong>possibility</strong>, capable of receiving every form and judgment, including vicegerency.</p>
<p>They retained knowledge of some conditions, but others escaped them. A condition of vicegerency is the <strong>actual appearance of all three grounds of comprehensiveness in justice and balance</strong>, so that none dominates or suppresses the judgments of the others. Yet angelic constitution and origin allow the judgments of necessity, simplicity and unity to predominate over possibility, multiplicity and composition.</p>
<p>A further condition is to appear under and undergo <strong>all ranks—spiritual, imaginal and sensory—and their requirements</strong>, giving each its due while remaining unrestricted by any of them. The angels are restricted to one rank and its condition: “None among us but has an appointed station” (Qurʾān 37:164). Another indispensable condition is relationship to <strong>all divine names</strong> by dependence, taking on their attributes, or realization. But angels do not participate, in the requisite way, in the names the Ever-returning, Pardoner, Forgiver, Giver of death, and similar names.</p>
<p>Among the greatest requirements of vicegerency is <strong>knowledge of all ranks, their inhabitants, their rights and judgments</strong>. The vicegerent stands between the one deputizing him and those over whom he is deputized; he receives from the former and gives to the latter. Without knowing the beings governed, their ranks and entitlements, he cannot fulfill the duty of vicegerency. The angels do not possess such knowledge in actuality, as will become clear.</p>
<p>Other faults included self-admiration and declaring themselves free of deficiency; observing their own worship and obedience; attributing sanctifying obedience to their own power rather than to the aid, strength, success and protection of their Lord; and presuming to object to their Lord and King. <strong>Eighteen blameworthy characteristics</strong> thus became manifest, though latent within them and unsuspected by them.</p>
<p>Iblīs was the cause of their manifestation and the one who induced them. The Real wished to purify, reform and perfect the angels by removing these imperfections, since they were parts of the being He wished to perfect, enabling them consciously to participate in bringing forth Adam, the most complete manifestation of perfection. The disclosure “I know what you do not know” (2:30) awakened their receptivity to purification.</p>
<p>Their earlier orientation toward producing the Throne, Footstool, heavens, planets, elements and generated beings, through the divine names' principal and subordinate orientations and conjunctions, before the earthen form of Adam existed, had been colored by their latent imperfections. When the warning awakened their capacity for purification, the original motion of love toward perfect self-vision appeared among the Keys, all principal and derivative names, and their angelic spiritual manifestations. After the celestial and planetary manifestations had become established, the angels turned—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p98" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p98"><h3 id="title-b2007-p98">B2007 p. 98 · Preparation of Adam and the breathing of the spirit</h3>

<p>—through the divine names and through their own realities and spiritual, imaginal and sensible celestial and planetary manifestations to the <strong>equilibration of the human temperament</strong> and the elemental form of Adam.</p>
<p>This form passed through four terrestrial conditions: <strong>earth</strong>, then <strong>mud</strong> when the watery element joined it and displayed its action and properties, then <strong>molded dark clay</strong> when air entered and contributed its qualities, and then <strong>ringing clay</strong> when the fiery element manifested its effects and qualities in the composition.</p>
<p>When its proportioning was complete through the operation of one of the two holy hands—associated with the manifestation of wisdom—the other creation began through the <strong>holy right hand</strong>, associated with the effects of power. Through it God breathed into Adam from His <strong>Supreme Spirit</strong>, directing the aspect of His comprehensive manifestation to govern this fully proportioned human constitution. He employed the angels, who were like the powers and components of that right hand, but without their own deliberate presence, intention or particular orientation being involved. For this reason the act of breathing was attributed to Himself in the <strong>singular</strong>, not the plural: “I breathed into him from My Spirit” (Qurʾān 15:29), not “We breathed into him from Our Spirit.”</p>
<p>When Adam's form and meaning were completed, he became the <strong>spirit of the constitution of the whole world</strong>, high and low, and a complete mirror capable of the Real's seeing His own image and all His beautiful names and lofty attributes through and within him.</p>
<p>The Real then began to perfect him. Before the actual perfection of his parts He perfected the <strong>form of their comprehensiveness through knowledge of the names</strong>. Knowledge of the innermost Essence is impossible, but knowledge of all the names is possible: “He taught Adam all the names” (Qurʾān 2:31).</p>
<p>In reality the divine names are <strong>determinations of the light of existence</strong> realized through meanings and realities, whether what bestows existence or what receives its bestowal. Words composed of letters that signify these existential determinations—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p99" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p99"><h3 id="title-b2007-p99">B2007 p. 99 · Knowledge of the names as knowledge of oneself and one's Lord</h3>

<p>—are <strong>names of those names</strong>. Relative to the spoken and written names the determinations themselves are the things named. By “He taught Adam the names” (2:31), what is meant is these realities as things named; the qualification <strong>“all of them”</strong> includes their spoken and written expressions. Farghānī notes that the Qurʾān uses demonstratives and pronouns proper to rational beings—“these,” “they”—with respect to these real names.</p>
<p>The Real thus made Adam know the reality of his own self: what his reality and existence comprise of names, attributes, divine and created realities, distinct in one respect at the second rank and not identical with the essential names established at the first. They are what those names truly designate, and it is upon them that the existence of the world depends. Through this teaching Adam came to know <strong>himself</strong>, and through self-knowledge, his Lord, in the sense of the saying “Whoever knows himself knows his Lord.” Thus his essence was perfected in respect of its <strong>comprehensiveness</strong>.</p>
<p>The Real then wished to unite in Adam the perfection of the whole and the perfection of its parts. He began perfecting the most particular of his components, the <strong>angels</strong>, now receptive because of the warning “I know what you do not know” (2:30). He presented to them everything He had taught Adam—what his self contained inwardly and outwardly, from creation and the Real—and said, “Tell Me the names of these if you are truthful” (2:31).</p>
<p>That is, if you are truthful in supposing you are qualified for vicegerency and in the inferences you have made from one thing to another, name the <strong>latent judgments of possibility within yourselves</strong> that led you to display factional zeal, reproach, assertion and egoism. Identify what is outward in you and what remains inward, what you have shown and what you have been unable to show because of the dominance of its realities; tell the names of the existential realities of your outwardness and what has been bestowed upon you in your respective worlds of the spiritual sovereignty of each thing.</p>
<p>Name also whatever belongs to the higher and lower worlds visible to you, according to its expression or distinguishing property; and name what is contained in Adam's self of divine perfections and creaturely properties. This knowledge is special to the <strong>vicegerent</strong>, who must be an image of the One who delegates to him.</p>
<p>The angels, restricted by their rank and constitution, were not guided to know what lay beyond them. They confessed incapacity and limitation, declaring in the language of their own formation: <strong>Glory be to You</strong>—no one knows anything outward or inward unless You have taught him, whether by nature or acquired instruction; and no one can oppose Your word, judgment, wisdom or knowledge, or resist the force of Your reproach and the consequences of disobeying You. “We have no knowledge except what You have taught us” (2:32), through our natural constitution—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p100" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p100"><h3 id="title-b2007-p100">B2007 p. 100 · The angels' instruction and the refusal of Iblīs</h3>

<p>—and original disposition. “Indeed You are the Knowing” (2:32), concerning the things You asked us about, by the judgment of placing that knowledge in one qualified to receive it.</p>
<p>When their incapacity became clear and they renounced what they had said and done, God returned to perfecting them through their <strong>origin and whole</strong>, saying to Adam: “Tell them the names of the realities named,” namely those named by Our essential, attributive, act-related, state-related and rank-related names, with the various things they bestow and to which they refer in angelic and other forms of existence.</p>
<p>When Adam informed the angels of them, they learned and became perfect <strong>through their whole</strong>. Their whole, in turn, acquired another perfection through the perfection of the parts. The Real reminded them of the truth of “I know what you do not know” (2:30), repeating, “Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and earth” (2:33)—the names whose effects permeate the heavens and earth under the creative command at every instant, through which Adam was formed and made actual.</p>
<p>“And I know what you disclose” (2:33) refers to the judgments of their existence; “and what you concealed” refers to the judgments of their possibility and the demands of their realities. These were all taught to Adam and deposited in his exterior, interior, heart, secret and innermost secret, because of his perfect receptivity, comprehensiveness and constitution. Through that complete receptivity the Real made him <strong>vicegerent</strong> in the perfection of His knowledge of Himself and self-witnessing through Adam, in Adam and every thing; in the love of His Essence unqualifiedly and under qualification; in His showing Himself through essential and name-related perfections comprehensively and in detail; and in His governance of the realm.</p>
<p>The angels submitted as parts submit to their whole and branches to their source. They recognized Adam's comprehensiveness <strong>except Iblīs</strong>, who failed to understand the meaning and failed to be guided because of his deviation and remoteness from truth. His fiery constitution impelled him toward elevation and pride, contrasting with Adam's earthen constitution, apparently the lowest of the low. Thus wisdom and the light of guidance did not affect him, and he refused to submit or recognize Adam's comprehensive reality, thereby passing from perfection to deficiency and abandonment.</p>
<p>He went further than refusal: he opposed, argued obstinately, and advanced <strong>imaginal arguments</strong> appropriate to his nature. He reasoned that, if comprehensiveness qualified Adam for election, he too comprised spirit and sense, while his own fiery nature was higher, older and subtler than earth and clay. How could the higher submit to the lower? His imagination veiled him, and his argument and resistance against the command drove him farther away. Earlier he had cast suspicion among the angels and incited them to dispute Adam's qualification—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p101" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p101"><h3 id="title-b2007-p101">B2007 p. 101 · Iblīs's misguidance and the possibility of angelic growth</h3>

<p>Iblīs had encouraged the angels to be pleased with reproaching and rejecting Adam's vicegerency, making claims for their own rank, and magnifying themselves, as in their saying, “Will You place therein one who will corrupt it and shed blood while we glorify Your praise?” (Qurʾān 2:30). The proof of this reading, Farghānī says, is that Iblīs's special fiery constitution has an aptitude for the appearance of these judgments, whereas the angels' own constitution does not contain the principles of corruption and bloodshed in the same way. Nothing appears from a created being except through what is present within it in actuality or potency. Hence it is appropriate to see Iblīs's suggestions as giving rise to the objection in the angels.</p>
<p>God said that Iblīs “was among the unbelievers” (2:34)—which Farghānī reads also through the literal meaning of <em>kufr</em> as <strong>concealing</strong>, in that he concealed the matter and misrepresented it to the angels before Adam's prostration. He led them to join him in thinking vicegerency remote and in criticizing Adam. Thus the impetus for the challenge, in his interpretation, was Iblīs's imagination and the predominance of its judgments.</p>
<p>May God protect us from ignorance that casts one far away, and from fragmented reckoning, and benefit us through knowledge, guidance and Godwariness. He hears and responds.</p>
<p><strong>This is clear evidence</strong>, Farghānī concludes, that <strong>angels, spirits, and intellects can progress and acquire increase</strong>, contrary to what certain philosophers have maintained. May God guide them.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" data-part-start="Foundation IV · Human reality and return" id="b2007-p102" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p102"><h3 id="title-b2007-p102">B2007 p. 102 · Fourth foundation: the human being and the two disclosures</h3>

<p><strong>FOURTH FOUNDATION: On the human being's ranks, successive stages, states, and the manner of return to his origin and final destination.</strong></p>
<p>It has already been established that the first thing determined from the true Unseen was <strong>essential real unity</strong>, equally related to unicity (<em>aḥadiyya</em>)—which removes all differentiated considerations—and oneness (<em>wāḥidiyya</em>)—which affirms them all. That equal relation is the <strong>first intermediacy</strong>, identified as the <strong>Aḥmadian Reality</strong> and the <strong>Reality of Realities</strong>, receptive to the disclosure of the One-in-Unicity to Himself.</p>
<p>The first self-disclosure, characterized by all-comprehensive unicity bringing those two relations together, is the <strong>Aḥmadian Light</strong>, alluded to in the reported saying, “The first thing God created was my light.” Here Farghānī explains “created” according to an original linguistic sense as <strong>determined</strong> or <strong>measured</strong>.
