This self-disclosure is the origin of all divine names to which lordship, rectification, kingship and mastery are attributed in relation to cosmic realities; it is their origin, source of their appearance, place of return and final end. Scripture alludes to this through “To your Lord is the return” (Qurʾān 96:8) and “To your Lord is the final end” (53:42).</p>
<p>This first self-disclosure contains <strong>essential perfection</strong> realized at the equal standing of the two relations <strong>without any condition</strong>, belonging to the first rank; and <strong>perfection through the names</strong>, whose outward manifestation, through the predominance of oneness, requires the <strong>second intermediacy</strong>, an image and shadow of the first, receptive to the second self-disclosure which is an image and shadow of the first disclosure. Oneness predominates at this second rank, and its included considerations emerge as differentiated forms, although their very realities were contained within oneness at the first rank.</p>
<p>As for essential perfection, its primary requirement is the complete <strong>disclosure</strong> (<em>jalāʾ</em>) of the most holy Essence to itself in all the considerations, consequences and properties of oneness, all included within oneness as the forms detailed in the ranks will appear forever.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p103" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p103"><h3 id="title-b2007-p103">B2007 p. 103 · Disclosure and self-vision; the Aḥmadian and Muḥammadan realities</h3>

<p>Through that disclosure and witnessing in the mirror of the first intermediacy at the first rank, the most holy Essence is <strong>independent of the worlds</strong> and of their successive differentiated manifestations, since it knows and witnesses them with all their properties and consequences while they are included within oneness: a witnessing of detail within a comprehensive whole.</p>
<p>The final requirement of essential perfection is <strong>complete self-vision</strong> (<em>istijlāʾ</em>) of the One-in-Unicity: its appearance to itself with a unity comprehending all the forms of its considerations after their return to Him—“To Him the entire affair returns” (Qurʾān 11:123)—so that the effect of none predominates over another. As with the earlier complete disclosure, its Essence contemplates itself in all-comprehensive unicity, but now through the <strong>perfected human manifestation</strong> analogous to the first intermediacy in its perfect justice and equilibrium.</p>
<p>This manifestation is both <strong>formal</strong> and <strong>intelligible</strong>. Its formal or corporeal reality is the purified and most balanced <strong>Muḥammadan temperament</strong>. Its intelligible reality is the pure, Godwary <strong>heart</strong>, which comprehends the Real under the first self-disclosure, precisely because of its complete comprehensiveness and correspondence to the first intermediacy. Neither earth nor heavens can contain this manifestation as such, because their determinations restrict them to particular meanings and properties.</p>
<p>The <strong>elemental form</strong> is Muḥammadan. Its inward meaning and reality, identical with the first intermediacy, is the <strong>Aḥmadian Reality</strong> of the Prophet. For the realization of the beloved singularity and uniqueness, the form of the one who inherits the <strong>taste of his sainthood</strong>, though not the reality of his prophethood, may also become a manifestation of this rank.</p>
<p>Perfection through divine names likewise requires complete disclosure and self-vision. Its complete disclosure has two kinds. <strong>First</strong>, the appearance of the second self-disclosure, in which oneness predominates, with the second intermediacy as its receptive mirror, containing seven fundamental attribute-realities determining the seven original divine names. Seven human realities are correspondingly determined: in each the trace of one name is manifest but concealed relative to the whole, while each includes all the others through true comprehensiveness because of its closeness to the first intermediacy.</p>
<p>Seven further human realities arise from them in the detailed, Cloud-like aspect of the second intermediacy. Their judgments are the reverse of the first seven—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p104" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p104"><h3 id="title-b2007-p104">B2007 p. 104 · Divine and cosmic differentiations and the completion of disclosure</h3>

<p>—from these seven second realities branch, within the Cloud-like Presence and its two sides—the Presences of Necessity and Possibility—divine name-realities to which action and efficacy are attributed, cosmic realities to which reception and being affected belong, and human realities emerging from one another as genera, species and individuals. All are <strong>forms of considerations of oneness</strong>, appearing as intelligible forms to the Real in relation, not as independently other beings appearing to themselves.</p>
<p>The <strong>second kind of complete disclosure through the names</strong> consists in the appearance of those forms as the effects of divine names and cosmic receptivities. The collective configurations resulting from their meeting are called <strong>creatures</strong> and <strong>others</strong>. An effect of the second disclosure, the all-merciful Breath insofar as it is bestowed, appeared as spiritual forms. Each spirit and each thing's spirituality became a manifestation of a consideration included within oneness.</p>
<p>The same effect then took <strong>imaginal forms</strong>, and afterward simple and compound <strong>sensible forms</strong>: Throne, Footstool, Gardens, heavens, fixed and wandering stars, elements and generated beings. The appearance of <strong>Adamic humanity</strong> completed the process of disclosure.</p>
<p>Every universal spirit-form manifests spiritually a universal name among the principal names or their universal derivatives; particular spirits manifest more particular names. Every universal imaginal form manifests one of those universal realities or names. Every universal celestial sphere or heaven manifests a principal universal reality in the sensory order, while its parts manifest their particular correspondences; each principal planet manifests a universal original name and lesser configurations more particular ones.</p>
<p>These cosmic manifestations bear the mark of <strong>otherness and createdness</strong>, so that each apprehends only creation and otherness, whether the object apprehended is itself or another of its kind. Through these forms each divine name realizes its <strong>specific assigned perfection</strong>, as the name's properties and effects become manifest within and through them.</p>
<p>Whatever is compounded from the elements at the various ranks of equilibrium among generated beings results from the effects of divine names and attributes, operating through their celestial and planetary manifestations and configurations under divine wisdom. Since in this sensory world things are predominantly related to their near or remote causes, only rarely does something occur without a perceptible cause. The divine names' effects therefore usually operate through celestial and planetary manifestations, each universal sphere manifesting a universal divine reality—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p105" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p105"><h3 id="title-b2007-p105">B2007 p. 105 · Cycles of particular perfection and the beginning of self-vision</h3>

<p>—among the original foundations, each moving planet manifesting one of the <strong>seven principal divine names</strong>. Each name and attribute possesses its own manifestation within a sphere through the configurations and connections of celestial bodies. During each period a particular sphere and a governing planet dominate, so that the judgments of the corresponding divine name and reality prevail over those of the others.</p>
<p>During that period, the genera, species and individuals of the generated forms associated with the predominating name arise, sustained also through the assistance of the other names operating through their subordinate celestial manifestations. In this way the <strong>particular perfections</strong> of all seven principal names and attributes are realized through their determinations and distinctions, as are the perfections of their celestial and planetary manifestations.</p>
<p>When the cycles of these seven celestial authorities end, each has manifested the kinds and instances of generated beings belonging within its scope. <strong>Complete disclosure</strong> (<em>jalāʾ</em>) thereby reaches its end.</p>
<p>A <strong>second cycle</strong> begins for each celestial and planetary manifestation, including its configurations and connections, this time to realize <strong>complete self-vision</strong> (<em>istijlāʾ</em>). The second self-disclosure, in which oneness predominates and which includes all the names and attributes in actuality, is to witness itself through the <strong>heart belonging to perfected human form</strong>.</p>
<p>That human form and its heart are the corresponding formal and intelligible manifestations of the <strong>second intermediacy</strong>, containing all divine names, attributes and cosmic realities and judgments, together with every divine and cosmic rank, while the trace of one of the seven names remains subtly present.</p>
<p>The second disclosure witnesses itself through that human manifestation and its own hearing and sight: <strong>differentiated witnessing within comprehensive unity</strong> when it witnesses itself in that manifestation, and <strong>comprehensive witnessing within differentiation</strong> when it witnesses what extends beyond it through the same faculties.</p>
<p>Such perfected human manifestations enable each of the seven original names, after attaining its specific perfection and the distinction proper to its effect, property and rank, to return to its <strong>principle of comprehensive inclusion</strong>. In this way it becomes a bearer of both sorts of perfection: its particular differentiation and its inclusive unity—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p106" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p106"><h3 id="title-b2007-p106">B2007 p. 106 · Adam and the seven perfect vicegerents</h3>

<p>—after which the second self-disclosure returns with these perfections to its original, <strong>the first self-disclosure</strong>. That return kindles in the first disclosure a renewed movement toward complete self-vision, and original love seeks its fulfillment.</p>
<p>The uniquely human attribute among all ranks is <strong>speech and articulated expression</strong>, outwardly and inwardly, for other beings share the other attributes in some ranks but not across them all. The first period of the celestial names' second cycles, directed to their name-related self-vision, therefore belonged to the manifestation of <strong>speech and the Speaking</strong>.</p>
<p>Through the original love, which moved the Keys and their subordinate names, spiritual, imaginal, celestial and planetary manifestations—now perfected in their own particular ways—the second self-disclosure, under the name of the Speaking, required the <strong>preparation and tempering of Adam's clay</strong>. All these manifestations were like the faculties and components of the hand to which his proportioning is attributed. Then He breathed into Adam from His Supreme Spirit without intermediary, as explained earlier.</p>
<p>Since the Speaking's influence predominated in Adam, he was singled out to <strong>tell the angels the names</strong>. His position within the intermediary rank was adjacent to the lowest heaven and the Moon, which manifest speech and the Speaking. For that reason the <em>Bayt al-ʿIzza</em>, locus of the Qurʾān's comprehensive descent, belongs to that heaven.</p>
<p>Adam's form, comprehending every perfection, became the origin of all <strong>drawn or outward human forms</strong>. The meaning and reality of Muḥammad, as the Reality of Realities, became the source of all <strong>human and nonhuman realities, meanings and spirits</strong>.</p>
<p>Corresponding to the seven original realities contained in the second intermediacy under its comprehensive equilibrium, <strong>seven forms of perfected humanity</strong> were determined: elemental and bodily in form, intelligible and heart-related in meaning, capable of receiving the second self-disclosure in all its comprehensiveness. Each contains all original, universal and particular divine names while bearing a concealed trace of one distinguishing principle.</p>
<p>That trace becomes apparent in the person's <strong>witnessings and spiritual tastes</strong>, belonging to the saintly aspect, and in his reports and the ordering of his earthly constitution, belonging to the prophetic aspect. Each of these seven perfected universal manifestations is called a <strong>vicegerent</strong>, a <strong>perfected one</strong>, and one of <strong>firm resolve</strong>, able to remain patient and steady at the midpoint between Real and creation: receiving assistance from the Real in his reality—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p107" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p107"><h3 id="title-b2007-p107">B2007 p. 107 · Law and scripture as the measure of the vicegerent</h3>

<p>—and giving to creatures under his creaturely aspect, without leaning toward either and neglecting the judgment of the other.</p>
<p>Every perfected vicegerent requires a <strong>universal measure</strong> coming from the Real, proportioned and balanced, preserving unity and justice on the creaturely side connected with his prophethood: first in himself and then in those who receive comprehensive existential assistance through him. This protects them against the judgments of possibility and the multiplicity of psychic and satanic effects. That measure is called <strong>the revealed Law (sharīʿa)</strong>.</p>
<p>When the measure is a <strong>universal verbal measure</strong>, comprising everything in the vicegerent's reality and existence—attributes, ethics, unveilings and spiritual tastes—in a form by which they may be perfected and brought to the Presence of the Majestic and Beautiful, whether in the comprehensive human form or in the differentiated human forms of his followers, among whom are the unjust, the moderate and those who precede others in excellence, it is the <strong>revealed Book</strong> bestowed upon each perfected vicegerent.</p>
<p>If the measure is more particular and partial by comparison, it is a <strong>particular law</strong> belonging to a prophet or messenger, originating from that universal verbal measure. Likewise, the realities and existence of prophets and messengers other than the perfected vicegerents branch from the realities and existence of those perfected ones. The latter are like <strong>principles and genera</strong>, while groups of prophets and messengers arise as <strong>branches and species</strong>, and their communities stand in a corresponding derivative relation.</p>
<p>The perfected vicegerents themselves, as to reality and existence, stand to the <strong>Reality of Realities</strong>, the Aḥmadian Reality and first intermediacy, and to the first disclosure—the inward aspect of existence and Aḥmadian Light—as genera and species stand to the <strong>highest genus</strong>.</p>
<p>During the sovereign cycle of each celestial and planetary manifestation one of the perfected vicegerents appeared. That cycle did not end before the prophets, messengers and followers branching from the reality of that vicegerent had appeared and attained their proper perfection.</p>
<p>Within each such period of one firmly resolved, perfected vicegerent, <strong>seven manifestations</strong> of the original seven divine realities must appear, with one particular judgment predominating in each, analogous to the seven <em>abdāl</em> of this Muhammadan community. Yet a qualification must be made. Whoever manifests the second disclosure while <strong>comprehending all the seven names</strong>, with only a concealed trace of one at the precise centre of the second intermediacy, is a directly appointed perfected vicegerent whose disclosures are essential. Whoever—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p108" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p108"><h3 id="title-b2007-p108">B2007 p. 108 · Perfected and derivative vicegerents; the return toward primordial equilibrium</h3>

<p>—belongs to the seven derivative followers, manifesting one original name under its distinctive, particular and articulated character in the Cloud-like Presence, is a <strong>vicegerent through</strong> that perfected one rather than directly, and his disclosures are through attributes and names, not through the Essence.</p>
<p>Thus each perfected vicegerent has seven derivative vicegerents; an analogous arrangement applies to the Muhammadan poles (<em>aqṭāb</em>). <strong>Every perfected person is a vicegerent, but not every vicegerent is perfected.</strong> Ponder this distinction between the station of perfection and the station of vicegerency. The perfected are few, the vicegerents many; and between two perfected ones there may be vicegerents occupying their place because vicegerency is close to perfection. Other subtleties of this arrangement are known only to the rarest of the great realized ones.</p>
<p>When the <strong>particular complete disclosures and self-visions</strong> of the second disclosure have reached perfection, and the cycles of its differentiated manifestations end by returning to it, that disclosure returns with its perfections to its origin, the <strong>first self-disclosure</strong>. The original love, colored by those perfections, now moves toward the realization of the first disclosure's complete self-vision, as previously explained.</p>
<p>The Keys orient themselves, under this condition, toward that perfection. The original and derivative names descend to the second rank with their special and comprehensive perfections. Together with their spiritual manifestations they turn toward fulfillment. At this point the sovereignty of the particular cycles—the cycles of the seven heavens and their planets—returns to the <strong>original, universal, unified cycle of the limiting Throne</strong>, and its comprehensive and balanced demand for a manifestation corresponding to the <strong>first intermediary</strong>.</p>
<p>The Prophet's reported words, “Time has revolved to the form in which it was on the day God created the heavens and earth,” indicate that return. On the day of their origination, dominion belonged to the unified, balanced cycle of the Throne, and its demand too was one and balanced. What appeared was a single, comprehensive, joined <strong>Supreme Element</strong>, the matter from which heavens and earth were formed and which stood in equilibrium among the four elemental realities—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p109" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p109"><h3 id="title-b2007-p109">B2007 p. 109 · Return to the universal cycle and the Muḥammadan temperament</h3>

<p>—the four elemental realities and their determinations and differentiations. After that joined matter was opened and the heavens and their respective cycles became determined, the sovereignty of the corresponding cycle passed at each period to one of them, for the wisdom already indicated. Differences in the judgments of these cycles, arising from differences in their particular receptivities, produced variations in calendrical reckoning, intercalation and the like.</p>
<p>When their periods came to completion, the judgment of differentiation returned to comprehensiveness and the sovereignty of the cycles returned to the <strong>Throne's universal cycle</strong>, which is the source of time. Thus intercalation and calendar manipulation came to an end, and time and its cycle once again followed the judgment of unity and equilibrium.</p>
<p>The time was therefore ripe for the complete self-vision of the <strong>first disclosure</strong>, the One-in-Unicity who unites <em>wāḥidiyya</em> and <em>aḥadiyya</em> without distinction. An elemental human constitution, unified and balanced, had to be determined so as to manifest the first intermediacy <strong>in outward form</strong>. A pure, Godwary <strong>heart</strong> then became determined within that constitution to serve as its <strong>intelligible form</strong>.</p>
<p>Under the impulse of original love the Keys moved toward this perfection, and the seven principal names with their universal derivatives, their spiritual manifestations, and their imaginal and celestial manifestations—each having already realized its own comprehensive and particular perfections—were oriented by the return of sovereignty to the unitary Throne toward the determination of the <strong>most balanced Muḥammadan temperament</strong>.</p>
<p>Existence became determined from the Presence of the first self-disclosure, descending through all ranks and their judgments and effects, in the manner proper to their unified, balanced and already perfected constitution, without arrest or impediment. That existential disclosure appeared in the form of appropriately balanced <strong>nourishment</strong>, which ʿAbd Allāh and Āmina consumed in the most suitable manner and at the most favorable time. It became seminal substance under the most balanced conditions; the effect of original love appeared in them as desire in a completely suitable state.</p>
<p>The two came together, and the blessed, auspicious seed was established in the womb at the most favorable hour and fortunate celestial configuration, as required by the original balanced cycle of the Throne, whose judgment pervaded the subordinate cycles. Every divine name, through its spiritual, imaginal and sensible celestial manifestations and their acquired perfections, undertook to nurture and preserve that most complete and balanced constitution throughout its stages.</p>
<p>After its formation, the <strong>Supreme Spirit</strong>, the most primordial and unitary, identical with the Supreme Pen—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p110" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p110"><h3 id="title-b2007-p110">B2007 p. 110 · The Prophet's development and the two cosmic books</h3>

<p>—under the aspect in which it appears as differentiated within the Tablet through the command “Write what will be,” and turns toward the world for its rectification, governance and nurture, became attached to this most completely proportioned temperament at the most perfect time.</p>
<p>Muḥammad appeared in the sensible world at a most auspicious moment, and at his appearance his light illumined the world from east to west, as his mother Āmina reportedly described at length. The first disclosure and the Keys of the Unseen, through their permeation of every universal and particular name and manifestation, then undertook to raise him from infancy to maturity.</p>
<p>The heat of his being <strong>sought</strong> prompted his withdrawal to the cave of Ḥirāʾ, while the sign of his being <strong>beloved</strong> ordered him to realize the secret of the night journey alluded to in “Glory be to Him who carried His servant by night” (Qurʾān 17:1). He reached the degree of perfection and supreme perfection beyond which no rank, final end, beginning or limit exists in prophethood, messengerhood and sainthood. Praise belongs to God alone for this care, sufficiency and perfect solicitude.</p>
<p>One of its most complete and universally beneficial effects was the determination of a <strong>universal, comprehensive, perfected verbal measure</strong> for him: the noble Book and wise Qurʾān, to which falsehood cannot come from before or behind, a revelation from the Wise and Praiseworthy. It sets out the <strong>revealed law</strong>, universal in its judgment and benefit, summarizing all laws concerned with perfecting bodily states through action and speech.</p>
<p>It also explains the subtleties of the <strong>Path</strong> (<em>ṭarīqa</em>), which perfects psychic and spiritual constitution through the rectification of character and knowledge of the soul's afflictions. It also explains the science of <strong>Reality</strong> (<em>ḥaqīqa</em>), namely knowledge of the Real, His beautiful names and lofty attributes.</p>
<p>Thus what descends from the Unseen to visible reality comprises <strong>two books</strong>: one of <strong>acts</strong>, the other of <strong>utterance</strong>.</p>
<p>The first, the manifest Book appearing through power and action, is <strong>the world</strong>. Every individual universal reality of it, considered apart from its necessary concomitants and dependents, is like a <strong>letter</strong>. Considered under its original receptivity to existence, it is like a <strong>name</strong>. Considered under its actual reception of existence through the request of preparedness, it is like a <strong>verb</strong>.</p>
<p>When a reality is joined to existence and its concomitants in such a way that createdness, actuality and otherness are signified, it becomes like a <strong>word</strong>. When such a combination expresses coordinated meanings indicating a single reality, as life, knowledge and will attributed to the reality, it is like a <strong>verse</strong>. When it includes the reality together with a whole rank—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p111" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p111"><h3 id="title-b2007-p111">B2007 p. 111 · The world as book and the Qurʾān as comprehensive expression</h3>

<p>—of divine names or cosmic realities and their judgments, it resembles a <strong>sūra</strong>. When it comprehends every universal and particular divine and cosmic rank included within the second determination and its intermediacy, it is a clear <strong>book</strong>, whose summarized practical image is <strong>Adam</strong>, together with the perfected vicegerents and messengers of firm resolve who preceded Muḥammad.</p>
<p>If that all-comprehensive combination includes <strong>the Reality of Realities</strong>, the first rank and the greatest intermediacy pervading every rank, so that only the single supreme Witness and His true inheritor can witness it, the result is analogous to the <strong>Qurʾān</strong>, whose summary and most comprehensive formal image is <strong>Muḥammad</strong>.</p>
<p>The second, <strong>verbal book</strong>, is the wise revealed Book that establishes the perfection of the aforementioned condensed book of acts. Its articulation differs according to the realities and principles contained in the second intermediacy. From each of these the second self-disclosure has a <strong>descent</strong>, with a universal manifestation governing that descent and a period of sovereignty proper to it. It then has a <strong>return and ascent</strong>, manifested by a comprehensive human reality: one of the perfected vicegerents other than our Prophet.</p>
<p>Each such perfected vicegerent has his own <strong>book</strong>, which establishes the perfection of his constitution and explains his central point of balance in every movement and stillness, action, statement and state, and indeed in those of his followers, people and descendants. Examples include the scrolls and books of Adam, Seth, Idrīs, Abraham, Moses, David and Jesus, peace be upon them.</p>
<p>The <strong>wise Qurʾān</strong>, by contrast, comprehends the judgments of all the original seven realities and governing divine names in an <strong>undivided unity of comprehensiveness</strong>. No characteristic effect of one predominates over the others. It was revealed upon the comprehensive manifestation of that same unity—our Prophet Muḥammad.</p>
<p>The Qurʾān establishes his <strong>supreme perfection</strong> and expresses the essential nature of his mediating equilibrium through all his sayings, actions, attributes and ethical traits, in his comprehensive Muḥammadan form and its differentiated manifestation among his people and followers from beginning to end. This explains ʿĀʾisha's statement when asked about his character: <strong>“His character was the Qurʾān.”</strong> Her knowledge and expert insight came from the lamp-niche of that all-comprehensive, unitary Muḥammadan prophetic Presence.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p112" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p112"><h3 id="title-b2007-p112">B2007 p. 112 · Each divine name has a point of equilibrium: wilāya</h3>

<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> Know that the essential and attributive names, universal in every respect—such as the inward and outward aspects of <em>Allāh</em> and <em>al-Raḥmān</em>, the Keys of the Unseen and the original principles, each containing all the others—and the names universal under one aspect but not another, such as their derived divine names in the number ninety-nine, then three hundred, one thousand and one, and one hundred twenty-four thousand, corresponding to the prophetic and saintly realities derived from these names: each has a <strong>point of equilibrium</strong> comprehending all that falls within that name's scope.</p>
<p>If such a universal name turns away from that point, it loses its comprehensive intelligible form and even the name by which it was designated; one of the partial names included within it comes to dominate and display its particular form.</p>
<p>This point of equilibrium is the <strong>point of sainthood</strong> (<em>wilāya</em>), since it is near to the unicity of the Absolute Unseen. The original linguistic meaning of <em>wilāya</em> belongs to the terms for closeness and succession: two or more things are adjacent with nothing alien interposed. Hence it is employed for proximity of place, kinship, religion and other relations; it likewise denotes proximity in the language of the realized masters.</p>
<p>Since all divine names are determinations of the self-disclosure of the all-merciful Breath, descending to realize the complete disclosure and self-vision described earlier, every kind of universal name has a particular manifestation in each cosmic rank: spiritual, imaginal, sensory, celestial and planetary.</p>
<p>Its effects in the world of generation and corruption ordinarily depend on those manifestations and their configurations, as effects depend on causes. Each manifestation possesses an <strong>intermediate, balanced point</strong> that is its <strong>heart</strong>. The judgment of the divine name's unity appears only within and through that heart. Only through that point can the name influence what lies beneath it, govern it, or turn toward perfecting it. Celestial and planetary manifestations determine the nature of time and its conditions and effects—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p113" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p113"><h3 id="title-b2007-p113">B2007 p. 113 · The balance of prophethood and the return from sainthood</h3>

<p>—time, as explained, resembles a form of the sensory rank, for each serves as the container and locus embracing all sensible things. Every container has a characteristic effect on what it contains, so that the contained thing appears only in conformity to the container's condition. The judgments and effects of time vary according to the governing cycles of the heavenly spheres and planets.</p>
<p>The <strong>unified, balanced central point</strong> of every time-conditioned manifestation of a principal universal divine name is the reality of <strong>prophethood (<em>nubuwwa</em>)</strong>. It is elevated beyond the other parts of that manifestation after its unity is established, and it informs others of the unity of the name manifested by that form. If <em>nubuwwa</em> is derived from the root meaning <strong>to announce or inform</strong>, it denotes this reporting; under another derivation it denotes <strong>elevation</strong>.</p>
<p>Every human being who serves as a guide to others derives his existence and reality from some universal leading divine name and its reality, from which he originates and to which he must return. Whenever such a human being is released from the bonds of cosmic manifestations—whether by disciplined journeying or by divine attraction—and returns toward his Lord, to the original divine name from which his reality came, attaining its unified <strong>point of equilibrium</strong>, identified as wilāya, he becomes a <strong>saint drawn near</strong>.</p>
<p>When this guide, having become a saint, descends again to the cosmic ranks and attains the temporal point of balance associated with prophethood, he does so to raise people or communicate to them the reality of the unity and justice of the governing divine name. Those whose existence derives from that name can then bring their states, utterances and acts into accord with its judgments and with the governing conditions of their time.</p>
<p>If he is a <strong>perfected vicegerent</strong>, his communication occurs through the wise book particular to him. If he belongs to a lower rank, it occurs through a particular law by which he himself worships or by which followers are authorized to worship through him. His authority comes from the Name from which his prophetic reality is derived.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p114" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p114"><h3 id="title-b2007-p114">B2007 p. 114 · The distinction between saint, prophet, and messenger</h3>

<p>If such a prophet is <strong>commanded</strong> to call a particular people and communicate to them the law bestowed upon him, that invitation and communication constitute a <strong>particular message</strong> (<em>risāla khāṣṣa</em>), and the one so commanded is a messenger to a particular people, like the messengers before Muḥammad. If he is commanded to address and communicate to <strong>all creatures</strong>, that is a universal message, and he is the universal messenger, like our Prophet.</p>
<p>Thus, in this exposition, the <strong>prophet</strong> possesses divine <strong>permission</strong> to communicate, but not necessarily a command; the <strong>messenger</strong> possesses a divine <strong>command</strong>, and is enjoined to call and convey. The <strong>saint</strong> likewise possesses a particular permission when he has reached the final station of stillness or fixing (<em>tawqīf</em>), or a general permission to act in the world when he occupies an intermediate station of directed disposal (<em>taṣrīf</em>).</p>
<p>If a saint descends to the cosmic ranks but does <strong>not</strong> appear at the central equilibrium of the manifestation called prophethood, appearing instead at some side or region around it, he is not a prophet or messenger. In proportion to his closeness to that equilibrium he participates in invitation, establishment and effective authority among the Muhammadan inheritors.</p>
<p>The descent of self-disclosure through divine and cosmic ranks has always occurred between <strong>comprehensive gathering and detailed distinction</strong>, or between union and separation. The first determination and disclosure possess real unity, comprehensive gathering and inclusion. Their differentiated aspect is <strong>relational</strong>, consisting of the considerations of oneness included within them.</p>
<p>Those relational considerations are gathered at the second determination and disclosure. Their subsequent differentiation appears as the multiplicity of known things and the relational multiplicity of the divine names. The <strong>Supreme Pen</strong> comprehends this differentiation. The <strong>Preserved Tablet</strong> is its articulated manifestation, including the spirits and angels. The <strong>primordial dust</strong> comprehends that further differentiation, while the Throne, Footstool and imaginal forms articulate it.</p>
<p>The <strong>Supreme Element</strong> comprehends this articulation; its differentiation produces the elements, heavens and generated beings through their kinds, species and individuals. The final, true comprehensive gathering of this differentiation is the form of <strong>Adam</strong>, whose differentiated aspects are the realities of the perfected vicegerents, prophets and messengers.</p>
<p>Every such person likewise serves as a comprehensive whole for those within his particular people, whether receptive or refusing. The true gathering of all this Adamic differentiation belongs to the complete <strong>Muḥammadan form</strong> and the still more comprehensive Muḥammadan reality—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p115" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p115"><h3 id="title-b2007-p115">B2007 p. 115 · Adamic descent versus Muḥammadan return</h3>

<p>—the differentiated aspects of that all-comprehensive unicity are the perfected vicegerents, poles, substitutes and all those falling under each such person within the Muhammadan community.</p>
<p>Adam, however, is the bearer of <strong>descent</strong>. Thus he manifests all divine names differentiated at the second rank when the inward existential self-disclosure descends there to realize name-related perfection, which requires distinction and plurality. He therefore gathers as source all human forms determined under the judgment of being last: “The human being was the last existent created,” as Farghānī reports.</p>
<p>He was ordered to descend from the Garden—where the whole conceals the parts and their differentiation—and taught the knowledge of the names differentiated at the second rank, the rank of the Real's outward aspect. He did <strong>not</strong> receive knowledge of the essential names proper to the first rank, the inward aspect, whose true realities are what the names taught to Adam ultimately designate. Their knowledge is particular to the <strong>Muḥammadan Presence</strong>.</p>
<p>Since every perfected vicegerent, and all prophets, messengers and communities under their scope, articulate Adam's comprehensiveness in descent, its judgment pervades them as they realize the name-related completion of disclosure and self-vision. Every such human guide first frees himself from cosmic restrictions and realizes the equilibrium of his original divine name; then he descends again into its manifestations at the point proper to <strong>prophethood</strong>, governing his temporal circumstances, showing the unity of his name through his actions, speech, character and states, and through those who follow him.</p>
<p>Thus, from Adam to Muḥammad, <strong>prophethood was outwardly manifest and sainthood hidden within it</strong>. This reflects the sovereignty of forms during descent and the concealed character of the names while their manifestations dominate.</p>
<p>Our Prophet, by contrast, is the bearer of <strong>ascent, return and restoration</strong>, in accord with “He who prescribed the Qurʾān for you will surely return you to a place of return” (Qurʾān 28:85). This means, to those who understand and realize the matter—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p116" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p116"><h3 id="title-b2007-p116">B2007 p. 116 · The Muḥammadan completion of return and the seal of prophethood</h3>

<p>—that the One who descended through you with the entire command, both Real and creation, comprehensively and in detail, so that through your reality, existence, meaning and form you became the unitary gathering of that whole, as an enacted and spoken Book, must return you to the <strong>highest place of return</strong>, the Presence of your Lord who is the final end of all things: “To your Lord is the final end” (Qurʾān 53:42).</p>
<p>He is thus the comprehensive manifestation of all divine names—essential and attributive—established in the first rank in comprehensive inclusion, and in the second in differentiated forms, together with their manifestations under the equilibrium of each in the descent of his light and its passage through every rank, culminating in the most complete Muḥammadan form.</p>
<p>Muḥammad is a comprehending whole for what became differentiated from Adam in form and meaning, as Adam was for what became differentiated from the cosmos. Through this universal, unitary Muḥammadan manifestation, each reality can be colored by <strong>essential perfection</strong>, comprising all the others without any remainder of the dominance of separate distinction or particularity, after first having received name-related perfection and its special properties and returned to the Presence that is the final end.</p>
<p>In him the realities of <strong>sainthood and prophethood meet in equilibrium</strong>, neither regularly predominating over the other. Farghānī refers to “We have sent you as witness, bringer of good news and warner” (Qurʾān 33:45).</p>
<p>Sometimes <strong>sainthood</strong> predominates, as in “Those who pledge allegiance to you are pledging allegiance only to God” (Qurʾān 48:10), or in the reported saying concerning an hour with God into which no near angel or sent prophet can enter. At other times the judgment of <strong>prophethood</strong> predominates, as in the declarations that he is a warner (Qurʾān 34:46; 46:9).</p>
<p>Since he bears return and ascent as Adam bears descent, the judgment of <strong>descent ends with him</strong>. Prophethood, connected with descent during the reign of the cycles and the communication of the perfection suited to each time, has been fulfilled. <strong>Prophethood is therefore sealed with him; there is no prophet after him.</strong> In his own constitution prophethood and sainthood remain together in equilibrium, corresponding to the primal equality of first and last, outward and inward, without essential dominance.</p>
<p>Sainthood subsequently proceeds from him and becomes distinguishable from prophethood in those nearest to him—</p>
<p><strong>End of stage segment:</strong> The distinction between the seal of prophethood and later Muhammadan saintly inheritors continues on p.117. Reports cited by Farghānī in p.116 have different authentication status; the translation reports his usage without treating every attribution as established hadith.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p117" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p117"><h3 id="title-b2007-p117">B2007 p. 117 · The distinction of sainthood from prophethood</h3>

<p>When this intelligible differentiation became determined, its meaning required a form within the sensory world. The judgment of that requirement spread among some of the Prophet's community until they asked him for the sensible miracle of <strong>the splitting of the moon</strong>. He supplicated, and through the judgment of his sainthood exerted an effect, so that the moon split outwardly and that intelligible meaning found complete manifestation in this form.</p>
<p>Just as the differentiated particulars of the comprehensive Adamic form were vicegerents, prophets and messengers, with sainthood included within them because theirs was the course of descent, so the differentiated particulars of Muḥammad's comprehensive reality and form, through those appointed as manifestations of his sainthood, are all <strong>saints and poles</strong>, with the judgment of prophethood included within their sainthood. They belong to the course of return and ascent, according to their comprehensive origin, the Muḥammadan reality in form and meaning.</p>
<p>Every universal divine name determined and differentiated at the second, divine rank had attained its particular perfection through the descent of its comprehensive reality within the second descent and self-disclosure; and each had returned with those perfections to the second intermediacy through the manifestation of a perfected vicegerent, prophet or messenger. But when the first self-disclosure, accompanied by its essential names, turned again toward the appearance of the most beautiful temperament, and the most perfect spirit and most equitable Muḥammadan heart became determined, carrying that first self-disclosure—his light in the first instance—and when the Prophet realized essential perfection, every one of those original, comprehensive names thereby acquired <strong>another return</strong>, more perfect and elevated than its first return with respect to its final destination.</p>
<p>That return takes place through a human manifestation, or several such manifestations, in the Muhammadan community. Such a manifestation is called <strong>saint, one brought near, knower, realized person, substitute, pillar, imam, pole or succorer</strong>, all comprehended under the name <em>walī</em>. In the first return, by contrast, each human manifestation had been called vicegerent, prophet, or one of the messengers of firm resolve, all comprehended under the name <em>nabī</em>.</p>
<p>Corresponding to every earlier vicegerent, messenger and prophet there is a saint among the Muhammadans; to every perfected one a perfected saint; to every seven substitutes associated with one of the perfected vicegerents seven Muhammadan substitutes following a pole; and to the earlier seal a corresponding seal—as Farghānī observes with reference to some unusual transmitted reports.</p>
<p>Since the Muḥammadan Qurʾānic book gathers <strong>all books</strong> and encompasses their meanings, it translates the meanings of all divine and cosmic realities, their states, the judgments of their differentiated details in the first descent for name-related perfection, and—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p118" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p118"><h3 id="title-b2007-p118">B2007 p. 118 · Why the Qurʾān and the Muḥammadan law suffice</h3>

<p>—secondly, the disclosure of their essential perfection through one complete and comprehensive manifestation, together with the differentiated manifestations following it, whose all-comprehensive form is Muḥammadan. It also articulates the judgments of that supremely perfect Muḥammadan manifestation, his states and character traits, and the ways in which his perfection appears. It articulates the conditions and characters of his differentiated followers, and the paths by which each reaches his proper perfection.</p>
<p>It also sets forth a <strong>complete, all-comprehensive revealed Law</strong> that safeguards the equilibrium of all these realities and manifestations, and the unity of the first disclosure and its names during their descent for the aforementioned self-vision. Therefore this book and law, by virtue of their complete comprehensiveness, inclusive exposition and sufficiency, make the establishment of another book or law unnecessary for every manifestation of the universal divine names. This is in accordance with the expression, “We have neglected nothing in the Book” (Qurʾān 6:38).</p>
<p>The Qurʾān thus comprehends every path and ruling, and encompasses every universal or particular matter occurring in existence from beginninglessness to endlessness, since it proceeds from the first determination and disclosure containing all eternal and everlasting judgments. Every rightly directing imam whose intellect, heart, spirit or innermost secret is illuminated by faith and the revealed law, by the light of special guidance, or by the light of witnessing, can understand, infer and draw forth from its expressions, allusions, indications and meanings the subtleties of the <strong>sciences of the Law, the Path and Reality</strong>. Thereby he guides those especially entrusted to him and, more generally, everyone.</p>
<p>As we have established, every comprehensive unity must have an articulation and differentiation. And every differentiated articulation must in turn have a comprehensive whole serving as its <strong>final summation</strong> and collective reckoning. Adam was such a summation of the world's differentiated particulars, and in turn an inclusive source for the differentiated vicegerents, perfected ones, prophets and messengers after him.</p>
<p>Muḥammad was the collective summation of that Adamic articulation, the comprehensive end of its human differentiation; hence <strong>prophethood was sealed through him</strong>. Yet since he, together with those in whom Muḥammadan sainthood became distinguishable from prophethood, is the formal comprehensive whole for the differentiated vicegerents, saints and all his followers, there ought finally to appear a <strong>comprehensive form of this later differentiation</strong>, a final summation through whom their sainthood is sealed, so that the last corresponds to the first.</p>
<p>This seal must gather the judgments of <strong>both modes of being</strong>, manifesting through him the effects of the worldly and next-worldly states, so that the judgments of the pole, vicegerency and perfection are completed through him in worldly existence, and the articulation of his comprehensiveness and the particulars included within his totality—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p119" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p119"><h3 id="title-b2007-p119">B2007 p. 119 · Constant existential renewal and dependence on a divine name</h3>

<p>—become completely outwardly manifest in the life of the hereafter, when judgment, command, sovereignty and predominance return to God, the One, the Overpowering.</p>
<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> Recall what has been established: the existence of every person, human or otherwise, is grounded in a universal or particular <strong>divine name</strong>. Once that person's quiddity becomes determined, descends through divine and cosmic ranks, and acquires individuality in the sensory rank, he needs at <strong>every instant</strong> an existential assistance (<em>madad wujūdī</em>) that makes his continuing existence prevail over his perishing. For perishing is demanded by the nonexistential nature of his quiddity.</p>
<p>The uninterrupted arrival of that assistance, together with the succession of instants, is what revealed language calls <strong>new creation</strong> (<em>khalq jadīd</em>), as in “Yet they are in confusion about a new creation” (Qurʾān 50:15). An example of the respective tendencies toward perishing and continuing is the continuous breakdown of bodily nourishment, with what decomposes being replaced at each moment; another is the oil consumed in a lamp's wick.</p>
<p>Divine names differ in the <strong>breadth and perfection of their encompassment</strong>, in narrowness and incompleteness, and in the universality or particularity of what falls under them: genera, species, and individuals. Each name possesses its special <strong>celestial and planetary manifestation</strong>. The universal manifestations possess dominance or subordination according to the sovereignty of their respective cycles.</p>
<p>Suppose a human individual's existence is first determined from the Presence of a name while the manifestation of a <strong>universal name</strong> is dominant through the rule of its cycle. If the name from which that person derives is one of the seven original universal leading names, the person's existence descends through the demand of the original movement of love, pervading the universal names and their manifestations, with their orientations and conjunctions, according to what that cycle requires.</p>
<p>He then passes through every manifestation and rank <strong>without being arrested or impeded</strong> in any rank. His journey is one. He first appears as nourishment eaten by his parents in the most balanced manner; it becomes seed without obstruction, the two seeds unite, and it settles in the womb. It develops through its stages there without impediment as all the names, through all their manifestations, provide assistance and nurture. He is born, reaches maturity and attains the rank of perfected men, becoming a manifestation of the universal name from which his existence first proceeded.</p>
<p>If, by contrast, the name from which his existence is determined is <strong>particular</strong>, the existence descending from it traverses the ranks with delays and impediments arising from the conflicting demands of opposed particular names and from differences in the judgments of their celestial and planetary manifestations. For example, a particular name may demand that an existent human become determined by a particular stellar configuration or conjunction—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p120" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p120"><h3 id="title-b2007-p120">B2007 p. 120 · Impediments during descent and the veils of the soul</h3>

<p>—so that there is prepared a vegetal or animal form from which the temperament of that human person, or part of it, is to arise. Yet an opposing name, whose ruling conflicts with the first, may demand the corruption of the vegetal or animal form. Each then returns to its origin or simple elements. On another occasion, another configuration brings about a determination, only for an opposed ruling to counteract it. This may happen repeatedly for one person.</p>
<p>The determination of that person's existence and temperament is thereby obstructed and delayed until he is finally freed from the effects of those impediments and his constitution appears. Each of the conditions of obstruction leaves within his <strong>human soul and temperament</strong> the predominance of judgments associated with possibility and natural effects. It makes him turn away and become heedless of his true Originator, exalted and holy, of what proceeds from Him in law, command, prohibition and matters of the hereafter, and gives rise to <strong>dark veils</strong>, constricting bonds, and distorted traits of character.</p>
<p>These are out of harmony with his <strong>existential secret, spiritual spirit, comprehensive unitary heart</strong>, and his animal soul and temperament; they stand between them and their origin, their source, and the road to their real perfection.</p>
<p>All naturally arising inclinations, appetites, sensory and imaginative loves, ambitions and hopes; the predominance of imagination, passing thoughts, conjectures, temptations, procrastinations of soul or devil; hatred, envy, greed, withholding possessions; even the inclination to <strong>unbeneficial sciences</strong>, from which the Prophet sought refuge in the words “O God, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit”—all arise, in Farghānī's account, among the judgments of these impediments.</p>
<p>So also do distorted beliefs not corresponding to truth, unfitting professions and crafts, and similar conditions. Every one of these deficiencies is related to a particular kind of impediment, and explaining them all would be lengthy.</p>
<p>Differences between seekers—some receiving an opening only after severe struggles, self-discipline and exercises while others do not; some quickly awakening and returning from habitual behavior to the continuous observance of worship, while others are slow; some being arrested at a station or state while others pass swiftly from one to another—all follow from differences in the <strong>number, strength and weakness</strong> of these obstructive judgments.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p121" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p121"><h3 id="title-b2007-p121">B2007 p. 121 · Spiritual pathology, revealed law, and remedies</h3>

<p>To know these impediments truly, to discern the distinctive property and effect of each in a particular seeker, and to know which <strong>utterances, invocations, inward and bodily actions</strong> will remove or oppose each one, requires a knower of penetrating insight, supported by realized witnessing and certain knowledge of the ranks of creatures and the divine names. Such a person must understand the secrets of the spiritual stages and stations because he has realized them in form and meaning—such as the prophets, messengers, eminent friends of God and great masters.</p>
<p>Everyone who aims for the door of nearness to the Real must remove these veils and their judgments. Just as celestial configurations and planetary conjunctions, insofar as they are manifestations of the Real's names and attributes, have effects in the world of generation and corruption because that world follows them, so <strong>human movements</strong>, as configurations and conjunctions of bodily acts and utterances through the person's limbs and faculties—each of which also manifests a divine name—have effects in the celestial spheres and above them, because the reality of the cosmos originally follows the reality of the human being.</p>
<p>Among these effects is the removal of the obstructive judgments just described; other effects include most forms of the intermediate world, the Gardens and the veils. Understand this.</p>
<p>In general, the <strong>revealed Law</strong> prescribes certain utterances, acts, movements and stillnesses which remove certain veils arising from the impediments and accidental conditions that overtake the existential outpouring, through the power of <strong>unity and equity</strong> pervading divine command and prohibition in those prescribed actions and words.</p>
<p>In particular, those learned in <strong>the Path and Reality</strong>, the eminent spiritual masters and physicians of these inward ailments, see through penetrating insight the sickness present in each seeker. They treat each disease with medicines and compound remedies drawn from <strong>invocations, works, disciplines, struggles, endurance</strong>, resistance to the demands of the soul, relinquishing personal choice, renunciation, divestment, unification and other practices that counteract the particular ailment in that seeker. The effects of these ailments extend from the seeker's soul into his spirit and secret. Treatment continues until the sicknesses disappear and the <strong>equilibrium of the spiritual temperament</strong> becomes manifest: this is the <strong>comprehensive unitary heart</strong>.</p>
<p>Keeping to the provisions of revealed law is like preserving health through an appropriate diet and drink in bodily medicine. But when a harmful quality or humor predominates and diseased material is stirred up, merely observing a regimen for maintaining health and balance does not suffice. Particular remedies opposed in their properties to the cause of the illness must be administered until the humors regain equilibrium. Only afterward can one rely on ordinary measures for preserving health. The same—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p122" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p122"><h3 id="title-b2007-p122">B2007 p. 122 · Why guidance by an experienced master is needed</h3>

<p>—holds of the predominance of the soul's judgments and veils, which are <strong>chronic illnesses</strong>. They require particular medicines of utterance, action, spiritual state and character until the unitary reality of the heart becomes manifest in health and equity. Once that occurs, keeping to the provisions of revealed law is sufficient to preserve the health of the heart through the effect of unity and equity that flows from the one divine command within those provisions—a truth whose determination will be explained shortly, God willing.</p>
<p>Consequently, among the most urgent matters for the seeking traveler, and among the loftiest goals and foremost conditions of the path, is finding a <strong>directing master</strong> and original source of instruction, learned in all three disciplines—<strong>revealed Law, Path and Reality</strong>—and able to discern the real character of the soul's diseases, the medicines that remove them, and the subtle ways in which appetite and greed infiltrate even recommended and permitted practices.</p>
<p>The seeker himself suffers from the illness of ignorance, heedlessness and the many other diseases already enumerated. He resembles a sick person who does not know his disease or its treatment, and who attempts to treat himself through his appetites and inclinations, ignorant of the disease, its cause and the remedy that opposes it. He may therefore suppose that something is a medicine when <strong>it is actually what destroys him</strong>.</p>
<p>We see people who think themselves seekers or realized knowers, filled with self-admiration, imagining that they have tasted or drunk of spiritual witnessing while never having smelled its fragrance or tasted a drop. They display <strong>acquired knowledge as if it were knowledge of unveiling and witnessing</strong>. Their tawḥīd is deficient; they imagine that permission to do as they please is unification, and that heresy is real gnosis.</p>
<p>Some have even supposed or claimed that they were <strong>the Mahdī, Jesus, a pole, a substitute</strong>, or the like. All this results from traveling by oneself without a guiding master, supposing that character discipline, ascetic practice and remembrance carried out under the dictates of personal appetite, desire and choice will benefit one or convey one to a divine Presence. But the Presence of the Real is exalted above becoming a place into which any comer may simply enter, or which anyone may perceive save <strong>one after another</strong>.</p>
<p>“One” refers to being one in oneself after one's attributes have been effaced; “after one” refers to following one person, taking no step on the path before him and placing one's feet after his. Thus a self-guided seeker's medicine can become his illness, and his treatment the very cause of his death. May God protect us and all sincere seekers from the evils of our souls, from their destructive conjectures and overpowering imaginations. Amen, Lord of the worlds.</p>
<p><strong>Chapter.</strong> Having now understood that the source from which divine names and cosmic realities arise is the <strong>reality of unity</strong>—in its inward aspect, identical with the Reality of Realities at the first rank, and in its outward aspect—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p123" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p123"><h3 id="title-b2007-p123">B2007 p. 123 · Intermediacy within the human constitution</h3>

<p>—the second intermediacy established at the rank of Divinity—know that this intermediacy, by virtue of its universality, centrality and comprehensiveness, pervades every divine name to preserve the gathering of its <strong>real unity and relational multiplicity</strong>. It likewise pervades every cosmic reality to preserve its intermediate position between necessity and impossibility.</p>
<p>The outward aspect of this intermediacy has a judgment of <strong>comprehensive inclusion</strong> and a judgment of <strong>differentiated articulation</strong>. In the first it is the reality of each perfected vicegerent successively. In the second, called the <strong>Cloud-like Presence</strong>, the realities of all other human beings arise from it and remain established within it.</p>
<p>Some of these human realities lean toward its central balance and the predominance of its justice. The realities of earlier prophets, vicegerents and messengers and of Muhammadan vicegerents, saints and believing followers below the perfected ones therefore differ in their degrees according to their nearness to or distance from its equitable intermediate reality. Others incline strongly toward the pole of possibility and the judgment of multiplicity, so that in this account the realities of unbelievers and hypocrites also arise and remain established within it.</p>
<p>Know that the <strong>most balanced Muḥammadan elemental constitution</strong> is the image of the <strong>first intermediacy</strong>, insofar as the comprehensiveness of oneness appears through it. His most perfect, all-embracing <strong>heart</strong> is the image of the very centre of that first intermediacy and its unitive joining of <em>wāḥidiyya</em> and <em>aḥadiyya</em>.</p>
<p>The constitutions of the remaining perfected vicegerents, messengers of firm resolve and poles among the Muhammadan saints are images of the <strong>second intermediacy</strong>, in its differentiated aspect, which is called the Cloud-like Presence. Their perfected and comprehensive hearts are images of the <strong>second intermediacy</strong> under its comprehensive unity.</p>
<p>The temperaments of those who are not perfected vicegerents are images of the effects of the differentiated Cloud-like intermediacy, insofar as they incline toward the side of possibility in greater or lesser degree. The constitutions of prophets, saints, believers and affirmers of unity are inclined more strongly toward the intermediate balance than those of unbelievers and hypocrites.</p>
<p>The hearts of those below the perfected ones are images of a <strong>particular effect</strong> of the second, comprehensive intermediacy, which through its equity and comprehensiveness pervades every divine or cosmic name and reality.</p>
<p>With this preparatory exposition in mind, recall how the effect of the all-merciful Breath descended from the highest cosmic ranks to the lowest, the <strong>sensory rank</strong>, and from its higher part still farther down to earth and its compounds, culminating in the <strong>human elemental constitution</strong>.</p>
<p>At each rank during its descent it put on a garment appropriate to that rank. In the first cosmic rank it clothed itself in a <strong>spiritual manifestation</strong> and displayed its properties and judgments; in the second it donned—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p124" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p124"><h3 id="title-b2007-p124">B2007 p. 124 · The descent into the human animal soul</h3>

<p>—another, <strong>imaginal manifestation</strong>, and displayed the properties, judgments and effects of that garment; in the third it put on a <strong>sensible manifestation</strong> and became manifest with its descriptions, effects and properties.</p>
<p>At each rank the locus of its descent was an effect of the <strong>intermediacy</strong> that is in reality the heart of the particular form in which the spiritual, breath-like outpouring had become clothed. This outpouring also possesses a <strong>comprehensive unitary heart</strong> embracing all that its particular effects and attributes contain. The reality of that unitary heart remains established and implanted in both the manifestation and what is manifested, even while these bear the judgments of the spiritual, imaginal and sensory ranks and forms.</p>
<p>By that heart the <strong>original disposition</strong> (<em>fiṭra</em>) on which all creatures are formed is sustained, so that every thing praises its Lord, and knows its prayer and glorification.</p>
<p>When existential assistance came upon each obedient particle of earth—answering “Yes” and “We come willingly” in its original disposition—for the determination of an elemental temperament within the range of human equilibrium, it traversed the cosmic ranks and took on their forms and judgments, as explained, until it appeared in the form of <strong>nourishment</strong>. That nourishment became a seminal drop in the parents, was established in the womb, and developed through its stages until the <strong>human temperament</strong> was completely proportioned.</p>
<p>Then, from within the <strong>pinecone-shaped physical heart</strong>, through the effect of natural heat within its innermost part, a <strong>subtle vapor</strong> arose. Its subtlety made it receptive to the animal faculty, and the vapor, by virtue of that faculty, was called the <strong>animal spirit</strong> (<em>rūḥ ḥayawānī</em>).</p>
<p>At this point, through spiritual breathing, an <strong>intelligible, governing spiritual effect</strong> was breathed into it from the spiritual spirit, either through an intermediary or without one. The result was a <strong>human animal soul</strong>, differentiated from other animal spirits through that spiritual effect.</p>
<p>Yet the effects of this spiritual influx, determined from the higher unitary world with its unity, equity and purity, were overcome by the multiple judgments of possibility and the animal spirit's properties, because of the sensory rank and the sovereignty of nature therein. This spiritual effect therefore became veiled from its origin, source and Lord. The all-merciful breath-like outpouring itself, being clothed in the garments of ranked judgments, properties of compounds, developmental stages and the previously described impediments, became veiled from its origin and original unitive transcendent judgments, and became heedless of them.</p>
<p>The <strong>human soul</strong> is thus a configuration arising from the coming together of the mist-like vapor, animal faculty and spiritual effect, distinguished from other animal souls by this last constituent. Yet even it became veiled from the original disposition of its earthly, corporeal particle, which had answered “Yes,” and from the disposition of the original—</p>

</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p125" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p125"><h3 id="title-b2007-p125">B2007 p. 125 · The veiling of soul, spirit and existential secret</h3>

<p>—spirituality, whose origins are the spirits and angels who do not disobey what God commands them but carry out what they are ordered to do. The human soul became veiled from both these original dispositions because of the properties of mixture, developmental stages, multiplicity, impediments and the predominance of natural and animal judgments, as the sensory rank requires.</p>
<p>It forgot its two original dispositions, turning away from them toward the pleasures, preferences and appetites proper to the immediate sensory life. Its condition resembles a sleeping person who turns away from stable sensible things toward fleeting images and becomes heedless of what remains through absorption in what passes.</p>
<p>The judgment of this heedlessness, sleep and self-absorption encompassed <strong>three realities</strong>: the reality of the existential outpouring or <strong>existential secret</strong>, the reality of the spiritual effect, and the reality of the human animal soul.</p>
<p>Because the judgments of multiplicity predominated over these three, their attributes and character traits became distorted, inclining either toward <strong>excess</strong> or toward <strong>deficiency</strong>, in accordance with their respective rank and constitution. The influence of the unitary, balanced heart within each of soul, spirit and secret became hidden beneath those judgments and inclinations, its effect absorbed within them. In some people it was virtually consumed, like the human form and meaning in those among the children of Israel who were transformed into another form.</p>
<p>This was connected, in Farghānī's account, with the original inclination of their human reality, when it arose within the Cloud-like intermediary Presence, toward the side of possible reality. He speaks of a rejection not based on an intelligible cause, as expressed in the saying: “Whom He accepts, He accepts without a cause; whom He rejects, He rejects without a cause.”</p>
<p>His interpretation of “Then your hearts became hard thereafter, like stones or even harder” (Qurʾān 2:74) is that “even harder” points to the near extinction of the heart and the loss of receptivity to the removal of its veils, while “like stones” points to concealment of the heart while some capacity remains for it and its effects to appear once the veils are lifted. The rest of the verse describes differing degrees in which that receptivity is manifested.</p>
<p>Whenever the judgment of a <strong>preceding divine care</strong>, termed eternal solicitude and alluded to in “They have a footing of truth with their Lord” (Qurʾān 10:2), appears in a human individual—because the individual's reality inclined only slightly toward possibility or did not incline away from intermediary balance at all—the effect of the innate <strong>light of faith</strong> may become manifest within that person, either through hearing or without intermediary.</p>
<p>He believes in his Lord and submits to His judgment. Thereafter his existential secret, poured forth upon his reality and attributed to it, may become drawn out of the very veils and conditions described—</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p126" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p126"><h3 id="title-b2007-p126">B2007 p. 126 · Attraction and the three necessary tasks</h3>

<p>—and freed from their fetters. The spiritual effect and human soul follow it in that attraction and in casting off the clothing of those judgments. This may happen through the effect of the saying “Whom He accepts, He accepts without a cause,” in accordance with the reported maxim that a single attraction of the Real equals the deeds of both kinds of beings. Such a person belongs to the saints whom God draws from darkness to light <strong>without effort or acquisition</strong> of their own.</p>
<p>Alternatively, the light of faith appears within the seeker and he sees his own essence together with its two manifestations, spiritual and psychic, as prisoners in the confinement of natural judgments and the effects of dark veils, clinging to dispersed secondary causes to attain bodily appetites and pleasures.</p>
<p>The <strong>all-merciful existential secret</strong>, the divine outpouring, then addresses its two manifestations and awakens them from their slumber of turning away from the real command and from obedience to the Mighty Compeller, and from their habit of seeking fleeting imaginal things and turning away from their source: <strong>“O my two prison companions, are separate lords better, or God, the One, the Overpowering?”</strong> (Qurʾān 12:39).</p>
<p>The human soul, inwardly and in its inward inwardness, then awakens from sleep and becomes aware of how much time it has wasted. It cries out in regret for its negligence toward God. It also senses the accumulated dark veils and firmly binding natural constraints of possibility enclosing it, arising from habitual actions, pursuit of appetites and personal choices.</p>
<p>It now understands that this awakening entails <strong>three necessary tasks</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>first</strong> is to begin the journey and return from the places where habitual judgments hold sway, and from the continual seeking of transient, perishing natural and animal pleasures and desires. This requires adhering to divine command and prohibition in every movement and stillness, in speech and action. Its initial journey relates to <strong>the station of Islam</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>second</strong> is for the soul in its inward aspect to enter a state of <strong>estrangement</strong>, leaving its animal residence and familiar appetite-driven home—the place where the multiplicity of its bodily and satanic deviations appears—and connecting with its inward Presence and the judgments of equity and unity belonging to angelic, spiritual attributes and character traits. This corresponds to <strong>the rank of faith (īmān)</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>third</strong> is for the soul through its secret to attain a witnessing that draws it toward the reality of tawḥīd, by being effaced from the judgments of veils and restrictions acquired during its descent and association with the various ranks, shaking the dust of its created effects from the hem of its truth. This corresponds to <strong>the station of spiritual excellence (iḥsān)</strong>.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p127" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p127"><h3 id="title-b2007-p127">B2007 p. 127 · The three divisions of the opening journey</h3>

<p>The first of these tasks—<strong>beginning the journey</strong>—is divided into <strong>three divisions</strong>. Each contains universal, important matters called <strong>stations</strong> (<em>maqāmāt</em>), since the soul takes up residence in each station in order to realize everything under its compass. The successive appearances in the soul are called <strong>states</strong> (<em>aḥwāl</em>), because they undergo change.</p>
<p>The soul, once affected by the aforementioned veils, possesses <strong>three orientations</strong>.</p>
<p>In the <strong>first</strong>, the soul turns toward governing the body, completing it and bringing it to what benefits it now and hereafter in the best manner, that is, in conformity with the revealed Law, through its faculties, apprehensions and organs. The journey and stations belonging to this orientation are called the division of <strong>Beginnings</strong> (<em>al-bidāyāt</em>). They prepare for the journey by correcting the soul's powers, balancing its outward instruments, and acquiring its inward powers and strength.</p>
<p>The <strong>second orientation</strong> is the soul's turning toward its own reality, its self, correcting its qualities, considering their consequences and stilling their instability. It is the threshold of the soul's entry from the outward to the inward; the stations of this orientation are therefore called the <strong>Gates</strong> (<em>al-abwāb</em>).</p>
<p>In the <strong>third</strong>, the soul turns toward its inward reality—that is, the spiritual spirit—and toward divine realities, asking its assistance in removing veils and receiving aid corresponding to the removal of each veil. This division is therefore called the <strong>Transactions or Dealings</strong> (<em>al-muʿāmalāt</em>).</p>
<p>There are three especially important stations in each division; the remaining stations supplement and correct them.</p>
<p>Within <strong>Beginnings</strong>, the first and principal station is <strong>repentance (tawba)</strong>: returning from disagreement to conformity, from natural inclination to revealed Law, from the outward to the inward, and from creation to the Real. Awakening, turning back and self-accounting are included within it.</p>
<p>The <strong>second</strong> is <strong>holding fast to the cord of God</strong>: attachment to God's command and prohibition, and founding every deed, word and state upon the revealed Law in certainty. It includes reflection, remembering, spiritual audition and holding fast to God by trusting all His names and attributes: through <strong>relation</strong> at the station of Islam, <strong>adoption of their qualities</strong> at the station of faith, and <strong>realization</strong> at the station of iḥsān.</p>
</section>
<section class="b2007-page" id="b2007-p128" aria-labelledby="title-b2007-p128"><h3 id="title-b2007-p128">B2007 p. 128 · Discipline, remembrance, detachment, scrupulousness and sorrow</h3>

<p>The <strong>third</strong> station of Beginnings is <strong>discipline (riyāḍa)</strong>: removing the unruliness of the soul by cutting off its familiar attachments, interrupting its habits and opposing its whims and desires. One of the greatest pillars of discipline is <strong>continual remembrance (dhikr)</strong>: in general, the remembrance <strong>lā ilāha illā Allāh</strong>, or, for the removal of a particular bond or veil, a specific remembrance taught by a spiritual director so that its effect on the darkness of veils may be stronger.</p>
<p>This remembrance must be accompanied by <strong>presence</strong> and the repelling of every passing thought, even a thought about the Real Himself, forbidding every distraction that crosses the mind and gathering all concern away from anything but the One remembered.
